emperors.bio_md:
# 秦始皇 · 主要事迹

嬴政以秦王之身，承数世耕战与变法之积，完成对山东列国的次第吞并，于前二二一年称「始皇帝」。其意义不只在「打赢战争」，更在于把「皇帝 + 郡县 + 书同文车同轨」等制度，推到前所未有的规模。

统一之后，他频繁出巡（见年表与侧栏地图），东至海上，南至湘水，北临边塞，以身体力行宣示「天下一人」。封禅泰山、刻石颂功，是权力的仪式语言；同时，严刑峻法、大规模工程与思想控制，也使「秦政」成为后世争论不休的标本。

沙丘之变后，帝位落入[[qin-er-shi|秦二世]]，帝国迅速失稳。数年后，[[han-gao-zu|汉高祖]]刘邦所代表的新政治力量入主关中，秦的制度遗产却以更柔性的形式进入汉家天下。后世如[[han-wu-di|汉武帝]]的封禅与开边，亦可与此页长线对读。

> 本地参考：点校本《史记》、谭图第 2 册、纪年表（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
As king of Qin, Ying Zheng built on the military-agricultural strength and reforms accumulated over several reigns to annex, one after another, the states east of the mountains, and in 221 BC he took the title "First Emperor" (Shi Huangdi). His significance lies not merely in "winning the wars," but in pushing institutions such as "emperor + commanderies and counties + a unified script and uniform axle widths" to an unprecedented scale.

After unification he toured incessantly (see the timeline and the sidebar map): east to the sea, south to the Xiang River, north to the frontier walls, proclaiming by his own presence that there was "one man over All-under-Heaven." The Feng and Shan sacrifices at Mount Tai and the stone inscriptions extolling his merit were the ritual language of power; at the same time, severe laws, massive construction projects, and thought control made "Qin governance" an enduring object of debate for later ages.

After the coup at Shaqiu, the throne fell to

bio_parts_en.label: Qin Er Shi, the Second Emperor of Qin

bio_parts_en.value: , and the empire quickly lost stability. A few years later, the new political force represented by Liu Bang,
, took control of Guanzhong, yet Qin's institutional legacy entered the Han order in a more flexible form. The Feng and Shan rites and frontier expansion of later rulers such as

may also be read against this page over the long term.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Shiji*, Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2, and the chronology tables (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 秦二世 · 主要事迹

胡亥在[[qin-shi-huang|秦始皇]]猝死后即位，在位短暂。史书呈现的主线是：深宫决策被权臣裹挟、刑法更苛、与关东烽火形成恶性循环。对图鉴而言，二世页的价值在于：

1. 展示「短祚皇帝」的信息密度如何组织；  
2. 与始皇页的继承关系对读；  
3. 作为秦末到[[han-gao-zu|汉高祖]]起兵叙事的跳板。

正文与年表仍以《史记》等通行叙事为骨架，细节争议处保持克制，待后续版本加「史说」旁注。

# 汉高祖 · 主要事迹

刘邦由泗水亭长轨迹进入秦末乱局，以沛公、汉王而终为皇帝。他的一生路线，几乎就是一幅「帝国真空如何被重新填满」的地图：沛县起兵、入关约法、楚汉相持、定都关中。

与[[qin-shi-huang|秦始皇]]对读：一人完成第一次大规模统一并塑造皇帝制度，一人在制度残骸与战争废墟上重建更可持续的帝国。与[[qin-er-shi|秦二世]]对读：可见「中央失能」如何把地方豪杰推上舞台。

本页 MVP 仅立骨架，楚汉细节、功臣集团与白登等事件可在 M1/M2 继续加密年表。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Bang entered the turmoil of the late Qin from the career track of a Sishui village head (tingzhang), becoming the Duke of Pei and then King of Han before finally ascending as emperor. The route of his life is almost a map of "how an imperial vacuum is refilled": raising troops at Pei County, entering the Pass with his legal covenant, the Chu-Han stalemate, and fixing the capital in Guanzhong.

Read in parallel with

: one man completed the first large-scale unification and shaped the imperial institution; the other rebuilt a more sustainable empire on the wreckage of that institution and the ruins of war. Read against

bio_parts_en.label: Qin Er Shi, the Second Emperor of Qin

bio_parts_en.value:
: one can see how "central paralysis" pushed local strongmen onto the stage.

This MVP page sets up only the skeleton; the details of the Chu-Han struggle, the group of meritorious ministers, and events such as Baideng can be added to the timeline in M1/M2.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉惠帝 · 主要事迹

刘盈是[[han-gao-zu|汉高祖]]与吕后之子，以太子继位，时年尚幼。他承高祖之后，萧规曹随，与民休息，朝局却从第一天起便笼罩在母亲吕太后的身影之下：长安城的营建、诸侯王的来朝、匈奴的和亲，莫不有其参决，惠帝本人以仁弱著称，史书对他七年治绩的记载，远少于对吕后临朝的叙述。

即便如此，惠帝朝并非空白。除挟书律，放宽了自秦以来的文化禁令；修成长安城，使新都第一次有了完整的城郭；与匈奴继续和亲，维持了汉初的边境休养。这些举措没有宏大叙事，却为后来的文景之治铺平了地基。

惠帝崩于未央宫，年二十四，葬安陵。身后吕后立少帝，临朝称制，刘氏诸王几遭屠戮，直到[[han-wen-di|汉文帝]]入立，汉家才重归刘氏正轨。史臣评惠帝，多言其「仁弱」，而就其朝政所积而言，亦可与文帝一朝作长线对读。

> 本地参考：点校本《汉书》卷002《惠帝纪》、卷003《高后纪》，《史记·吕太后本纪》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Ying was the son of

and Empress Lü. He succeeded to the throne as heir apparent while still young, keeping the statutes of Xiao He and the policies of Cao Shen and resting the people. Yet from the first day his reign stood in the shadow of his mother, Empress Dowager Lü: the building of Chang'an, the visits of the feudatory kings, and the marriage alliance with the Xiongnu were all decided with her participation. The emperor himself was known for gentleness and weakness, and the histories tell us far less about his seven years of rule than about Lü's regency.

His reign was not, however, a blank. The repeal of the law against private possession of books relaxed the cultural prohibitions inherited from Qin. The completion of the walls of Chang'an gave the new capital its first full circuit of fortifications. And the continued marriage alliance with the Xiongnu preserved the frontier quiet on which early Han rested. None of these measures made a great narrative, but together they prepared the ground for the celebrated Wen-Jing recovery.

Emperor Hui died in the Weiyang Palace at the age of twenty-four and was buried at Anling. After his death Lü enthroned a young emperor and assumed the regency in her own right; the Liu kings were nearly destroyed one by one, until the accession of

returned the House of Han to its proper line. The historians called Hui "gentle and weak," yet in what his reign accumulated, he may be read against Emperor Wen's over the long term.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hanshu*, ch. 2 (Benji of Emperor Hui) and ch. 3 (Benji of Empress Lü), the *Shiji* "Basic Annals of Empress Lü," and Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 前少帝 · 主要事迹

前少帝刘恭是吕后以「惠帝后宫子」之名立起来的幼帝：[[han-hui-di|汉惠帝]]崩后，吕后临朝称制，立其后宫子为帝以续汉统，实权尽在吕氏。这个名分自始便有争议——朝臣心知他未必是惠帝血胤，史书也以「吕太后本纪」而非少帝本纪记其事。

他在位的四年，是吕氏权势登顶的四年：高后元年王诸吕，封吕氏为王，直破[[han-gao-zu|高祖]]的白马之约；高后称制下的法令亦随之调整。少帝本人不过系年而已，朝政皆出吕后。

少帝渐长，自知非皇后所生，口出怨言，遂于高后四年被幽杀，吕后更立恒山王刘弘，即后少帝。四年之间，汉家帝座两易其主而皆由吕氏摆布，直到[[han-wen-di|汉文帝]]入立，刘氏才算真正收回帝权。史家于前少帝多存名分之疑，图鉴故以「准帝」立页。

> 本地参考：点校本《史记·吕太后本纪》、《汉书》卷003《高后纪》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Gong, the Former Young Emperor, was the child ruler raised by Empress Lü under the fiction of being a son of the harem of

. After Hui died, Lü took the regency and enthroned one of his harem sons to continue the Han line, while all real power rested with the Lü house. The legitimacy of the arrangement was doubtful from the start — the court knew the boy was probably not of Hui's blood, and the histories record his reign not in his own annals but in the "Basic Annals of Empress Lü."

His four years were the apex of Lü power: in the first year of the regency the Lü were enfeoffed as kings, breaking the White Horse Covenant of

, and the laws were adjusted to the regency's taste. The young emperor was no more than a date in the annals.

Growing up, he learned he was not the empress's son and spoke resentfully; in the fourth year of the regency he was imprisoned and slain, and Liu Hong, king of Hengshan, was enthroned in his place — the Later Young Emperor. Within four years the Han throne changed hands twice, both times at Lü's pleasure, until the accession of

returned real sovereignty to the Liu house. The histories leave the Former Young Emperor's legitimacy an open question; this gazetteer therefore lists him as a quasi-emperor.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Shiji*, "Basic Annals of Empress Lü," and the *Hanshu*, ch. 3 (Benji of Empress Lü); Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后少帝 · 主要事迹

后少帝刘弘是吕后幽杀前少帝后所立，名义上的汉家第四位皇帝。他承袭的仍是吕氏称制的政局：名分存疑，实权在太后，[[han-qian-shao|前少帝]]的下场就是悬在他头上的先例。

高后七年，赵王友幽死，诸吕与刘氏的积怨终于表面化。高后八年七月，吕太后崩，长久压抑的矛盾即刻爆发：太尉周勃入北军，与丞相陈平定计，尽诛诸吕，随后以「少帝及诸王皆非惠帝子」为由废杀后少帝，迎代王[[han-wen-di|刘恒]]入长安即位。

后少帝在位四年，史书几乎没有留下他自己的任何事迹——他存在的意义，就是吕氏称制的最后一枚图章。诸吕既灭，这枚图章连同两个少帝一起被历史抹去，汉统由此重归刘氏。他的悲剧与文帝的即位互为表里：一个是称制终局的注脚，一个是新朝局的起点。

> 本地参考：点校本《史记·吕太后本纪》、《汉书》卷003《高后纪》、卷004《文帝纪》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Hong, the Later Young Emperor, was enthroned after Empress Lü had the Former Young Emperor slain — nominally the fourth emperor of Han, inheriting the same regime of Lü regency: his title doubtful, real power in the empress dowager's hands, and the fate of

hanging over him.

In the seventh year of the regency, King You of Zhao was starved to death, and the accumulated hatred between the Lü clan and the Liu house broke into the open. In the eighth year, the empress dowager died, and the long-suppressed conflict exploded at once: Grand Commandant Zhou Bo took the Northern Army, and with Chancellor Chen Ping he destroyed the entire Lü clan; declaring that "the young emperor and the kings are no sons of Emperor Hui," they slew the Later Young Emperor and summoned the king of Dai,

, to Chang'an.

In his four years the histories record almost nothing of the Later Young Emperor himself — his whole existence was the last seal of the Lü regency. With the Lü destroyed, that seal and both young emperors were wiped from the record together, and the Han succession returned to the Liu house. His tragedy and Emperor Wen's accession are two sides of one coin: the footnote to a regency's end, and the beginning of a new order.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Shiji*, "Basic Annals of Empress Lü," and the *Hanshu*, ch. 3 and ch. 4 (Benji of Empress Lü and of Emperor Wen); Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉文帝 · 主要事迹

刘恒是高祖庶子，封代王，都中都，在代十七年，以恭谨闻。高后八年，诸吕既诛，功臣集团迎立代王：他一度迟疑，经左右劝进，至渭桥受天子玺，入未央宫即皇帝位。以「外藩入继」之身，开启此后二十三年的文景之治。

文帝治国以恭俭宽仁为纲：即位即除诽谤妖言法，广开言路；十三年因缇萦上书而除肉刑，更定法律；同年免天下田租；尝欲作露台，闻需百金而罢，说「百金，中人十家之产也」。本纪赞称其在位二十三年，宫室苑囿无所增益，专务以德化民。匈奴入边时，他欲自征为太后所止，遂以遣将屯边、和亲羁縻为主，细柳劳军一幕，留下识将用人的名场面。

后七年崩，遗诏天下短丧薄葬，霸陵因山为陵，终其恭俭之一贯。太子[[han-jing-di|汉景帝]]即位，承其政风，遂有「文景之治」之称；汉家休养生息的底子，直到[[han-wu-di|汉武帝]]朝才转为开边进取。史臣以文帝与高祖[[han-gao-zu|汉高祖]]、景帝并论，后世更以「三代以下称贤君，必首推文景」为定评。

> 本地参考：点校本《汉书》卷004《文帝纪》、《刑法志》，《史记·孝文本纪》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Heng was a lesser son of Gaozu, enfeoffed as King of Dai with his seat at Zhongdu, where he lived seventeen years known for caution. In the eighth year of Empress Lü, with the Lü clan destroyed, the meritorious ministers summoned him: he hesitated at first, and only after persuasion from his attendants crossed the Wei Bridge, received the imperial seal, and entered the Weiyang Palace to take the throne. Entering the succession from an outer fief, he opened the twenty-three years known as the Wen-Jing recovery.

He governed by frugality, leniency, and benevolence: immediately on accession he repealed the law against slander and seditious speech, opening the channels of remonstrance; in the thirteenth year, moved by Tiying's petition, he abolished mutilation punishments and revised the law; that same year he remitted the land tax throughout the realm; once, planning a terrace, he abandoned it on learning it would cost a hundred jin of gold, saying, "A hundred jin is the estate of ten middle households." The historian's eulogy says that in twenty-three years he added nothing to his palaces, gardens, or parks, attending wholly to transforming the people by virtue. When the Xiongnu raided the frontier he wished to campaign in person, but the empress dowager stopped him; he relied on posted generals and the marriage alliance to hold the border — the scene of his visit to the camp at Xiliu leaving the famous exchange with the "true general" Zhou Yafu.

He died in the later seventh year; his will ordered brief mourning and a frugal burial for all the realm, and the Baling mound was hewn into the hillside — frugality maintained to the end. His heir
continued his course, hence the name "Wen-Jing recovery"; the foundations of Han's recuperation held until the reign of
turned to frontier expansion. Later historians ranked Wen with

and Emperor Jing, and after the Three Dynasties he became the standard of the good ruler.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hanshu*, ch. 4 (Benji of Emperor Wen) and the "Treatise on Punishment and Law," the *Shiji* "Basic Annals of Emperor Wen," and Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). emperors.bio_md:
# 汉景帝 · 主要事迹

刘启是[[han-wen-di|汉文帝]]之子，以太子继位。他承文帝休养之政，减笞轻刑，本可平稳守成，却因削藩一事掀起汉初最大的内乱——七国之乱，又以铁腕平之，把中央与诸侯王的权力天平彻底扳向长安。

乱起于御史大夫晁错的削藩之议：削吴楚支郡，吴王濞、楚王戊等七国以「诛晁错」为名举兵西向。景帝一度听袁盎言，斩晁错于东市以谢吴楚，而吴楚兵不止，方知乱意不在错。此后倚梁孝王城守睢阳，任周亚夫坚壁昌邑、断吴粮道，三月破吴楚，七国皆平。经此一役，汉初分封格局名存实变，中央集权为之奠定。

平乱之后的景帝朝并不太平：废栗太子，立胶东王[[han-wu-di|刘彻]]；临江王荣被征自杀；功高震主的周亚夫终以下狱绝食而亡。史家于此多有微词，谓其刻薄寡恩、少文帝之宽仁，然就制度后果而言，削藩与集权正是武帝盛世的前提。

后三年正月，景帝崩于未央宫，太子彻即位。文景两代四十年的休养生息，至此交棒到中国历史上最具扩张性的皇帝手中；「文景之治」作为汉家基业的代名词，也在[[han-gao-zu|汉高祖]]开国与武帝开边之间，成为承上启下的枢纽。

> 本地参考：点校本《汉书》卷005《景帝纪》、卷006《武帝纪》、《晁错传》，《史记》吴王濞列传、绛侯世家、梁孝王世家，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Qi was the son of

and succeeded as heir apparent. He continued Wen's policy of rest, easing flogging and lightening punishment, and might have reigned in quiet continuity — until his plan to trim the feudatories touched off the greatest civil war of early Han, the Revolt of the Seven States, which he then suppressed with an iron hand, tipping the balance between throne and feudatories decisively toward Chang'an.

The revolt began with the trimming plan of Censor-in-Chief Chao Cuo: cutting the commanderies of Wu and Chu, the kings of Wu and Chu and five other states rose and marched west under the slogan "execute Chao Cuo." Persuaded by Yuan Ang, Emperor Jing had Chao Cuo beheaded at the East Market to appease the rebels; the armies pressed on regardless, and the court saw that the revolt was never about Chao Cuo. Thereafter Jing leaned on Prince Xiao of Liang holding Suiyang, and entrusted Zhou Yafu, who held fast at Changyi, cut Wu's grain route, and broke Wu and Chu within three months; all seven states were settled. After that war, the enfeoffment order of early Han was changed in substance, and centralization was secured.

The years after the revolt were not tranquil: the heir of the Li clan was set aside in favor of Jiaodong's king

; Rong, the deposed prince of Linjiang, was summoned and died by his own hand; and Zhou Yafu, whose merit now overshadowed the throne, ended in prison, starving himself to death on the fifth day. The historians censured the emperor here — cold and ungrateful, they said, and lacking Wen's generosity — yet in institutional terms, the trimming of the feudatories and the concentration of power were exactly the precondition of Emperor Wu's golden age.

In the first month of the later third year, Emperor Jing died in the Weiyang Palace and Crown Prince Che succeeded. Four decades of Wen-Jing recuperation now passed into the hands of the most expansionist emperor in Chinese history; and "the Wen-Jing recovery," the byword for the House of Han's foundations, became the hinge between

's founding and Emperor Wu's frontier expansion.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hanshu*, ch. 5 (Benji of Emperor Jing), ch. 6 (Benji of Emperor Wu), and the biography of Chao Cuo; the *Shiji* biography of the King of Wu, the House of Zhou Bo, and the House of Liang; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). # 汉武帝 · 主要事迹

刘彻在位时间之长、年号之繁、开拓之广，使他成为读西汉史几乎绕不开的枢纽。本页以《汉书·武帝纪》为年表主线，辅以《史记》相关篇与《资治通鉴》编年（本地参考库已备）。

他强化中央集权、尊崇儒术、经营北边与西域，又留下边防工程、财政压力与晚年政策调整等复杂遗产。与[[qin-shi-huang|秦始皇]]对读：一人完成第一次大规模统一并定皇帝之制，一人把统一帝国的武功、礼仪与财政推到新高度。与[[han-gao-zu|汉高祖]]对读：可见汉家从草创到极盛的跨度。

bio_parts_en.value:
The length of Liu Che's reign, the abundance of his era names, and the breadth of his expansion make him a pivot that no reader of Western Han history can bypass. This page takes the "Annals of Emperor Wu" in the Book of Han as its chronological spine, supplemented by relevant chapters of the Records of the Grand Historian and the chronicle of the Zizhi Tongjian (available in the local reference library).

He strengthened central authority, exalted Confucian learning, and developed the northern frontier and the Western Regions, leaving a complex legacy of border defenses, fiscal strain, and a late-reign change of course. Read alongside

: one man completed the first great unification and fixed the institution of the emperor; the other carried the unified empire's military reach, ritual order, and fiscal apparatus to new heights. Read alongside
: one sees the span of the Han house from its rough founding to its full zenith.

emperors.summary: 八岁即位，霍光辅政，盐铁之议、轻徭薄赋，与民休息；年二十一崩而无嗣。
emperors.summary_en: Ascending at eight with Huo Guang as regent, he brought the Salt and Iron Debate, light corvée and taxes, and rest for the people; he died at twenty-one without issue.

timeline.title: 钩弋子生
timeline.summary: 武帝少子，母赵婕妤（钩弋夫人）；生年史无系日，此据即位年岁反推。
timeline.summary_en: The youngest son of Emperor Wu, by Lady Zhao, the Hook-Yi Lady; the exact year is unrecorded and back-calculated from his age at accession.

timeline.title: 立太子并即位
timeline.summary: 武帝疾病，立弗陵为太子，霍光受遗诏辅政；明日武帝崩，太子即皇帝位。
timeline.summary_en: With Emperor Wu ill, Fuling was made heir apparent and Huo Guang received the testamentary charge; the next day Wu died and the heir took the throne.

timeline.title: 益州廉头姑缯反
timeline.summary: 益州廉头、姑缯民反，遣吕破胡募吏民及发犍为、蜀郡兵击破之。
timeline.summary_en: The Lientou and Guzeng peoples of Yizhou revolted; Lü Poho was sent to levy men and troops from Qianwei and Shu commanderies and crushed them.

timeline.title: 盐铁会议
timeline.summary: 问郡国贤良文学民所疾苦，议罢盐铁酒榷均输，后罢榷酤。
timeline.summary_en: The worthy and literary men of the commanderies were asked about the people's grievances; the debate over the salt, iron, liquor monopoly, and equal transport led to abolition of the liquor monopoly.

timeline.title: 燕王旦上官桀谋反
timeline.title_en: Plot of the King of Yan and Shangguan Jie
timeline.summary: 燕王旦与上官桀、桑弘羊等谋杀霍光废帝，事败族诛，旦自杀。
timeline.summary_en: The king of Yan, Shangguan Jie, Sang Hongyang, and others plotted to kill Huo Guang and depose the emperor; the plot failed, the plotters were executed with their clans, and the king killed himself.

timeline.title: 霍光权固
timeline.summary: 诛反者后霍光专制朝事，昭帝「委任霍光」。
timeline.summary_en: After the purge Huo Guang dominated the court, the emperor entrusting everything to him.

timeline.title: 傅介子斩楼兰王
timeline.title_en: Fu Jiezi Slays the King of Loulan
timeline.summary: 平乐监傅介子使西域，计斩楼兰王安归，更名其国为鄯善。
timeline.summary_en: Fu Jiezi, superintendent of Pingle, went to the Western Regions, slew the Loulan king Angui by stratagem, and renamed the state Shanshan.

timeline.title: 昭帝崩
timeline.summary: 崩，年二十一，无嗣；大将军霍光等议所立。
timeline.summary_en: He died at twenty-one without issue; General-in-Chief Huo Guang and the others deliberated on a successor.

timeline.title: 立昌邑王贺
timeline.summary: 迎昌邑王贺即位。
timeline.summary_en: Prince He of Changyi was summoned and enthroned.

timeline.title: 废昌邑王
timeline.summary: 贺即位二十七日，行淫乱，霍光与群臣奏皇太后废之。
timeline.summary_en: Twenty-seven days into his reign He behaved dissolutely; Huo Guang and the ministers petitioned the empress dowager to depose him.

timeline.title: 迎立宣帝
timeline.title_en: Emperor Xuan Called to the Throne
timeline.summary: 光等奏立武帝曾孙病已，是为孝宣皇帝。
timeline.summary_en: Huo Guang and the others memorialized to raise Emperor Wu's great-grandson Bingyi, the Emperor Xuan.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉昭帝 · 主要事迹

刘弗陵是[[han-wu-di|汉武帝]]少子，母钩弋夫人。后元二年，武帝疾病，立八岁的弗陵为太子，以大司马大将军霍光受遗诏辅政；武帝既崩，太子即位。一个八岁的皇帝面对的是武帝末年虚耗的海内、猜忌的宗室和虎视眈眈的辅臣——而昭帝朝竟在霍光的执掌下平稳度过十三年，史称「知时务之要」。

昭帝朝的政策主线是休养生息：始元六年二月，诏郡国举贤良文学问民疾苦，围绕盐铁酒榷均输展开辩论，即盐铁会议，会后罢榷酤；轻徭薄赋，与民休息，接续文景遗风。边防方面，元凤四年傅介子使西域，计斩楼兰王安归，更名其国为鄯善，西域方向保持了汉家的声威。

朝局并不平静。始元年间燕王旦勾结上官桀、桑弘羊等，谋诛霍光废帝；昭帝亲察其诈，事败，诸人族诛，霍光遂专制朝事。关于昭帝本人，史载他早慧而明于判狱，但十四岁后权力实际尽归霍光，他在位后期的形象，更多是辅政制度的背景板。

元平元年四月，昭帝崩，年二十一，无嗣。霍光先迎立[[han-changyi|昌邑王贺]]，贺在位二十七日以行淫乱被废，复立武帝曾孙[[han-xuan-di|汉宣帝]]。昭帝一朝所积累的休养政策与辅政结构，延续为昭宣之治，成为西汉中叶最后的安定时代。

> 本地参考：点校本《汉书》卷007《昭帝纪》、卷008《宣帝纪》，《霍光传》、《傅介子传》、《武五子传》，《盐铁论》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Fuling was the youngest son of

, by the Hook-Yi Lady. In the second year of the Later era, with Emperor Wu ill, the eight-year-old Fuling was made heir apparent, and General-in-Chief Huo Guang received the testamentary charge as regent; when Wu died, the heir took the throne. An eight-year-old emperor faced the realm drained by the late campaigns of Wu's reign, a jealous royal house, and watchful regents — and yet the Zhao reign passed thirteen years in stability under Huo Guang's hand. The historians said he "knew the essentials of the times."

The policy line of his reign was rest and recuperation: in the second month of the sixth Shiyuan year he ordered the commanderies to recommend worthy and literary men and asked them about the people's grievances, opening the debate over the salt, iron, and liquor monopolies and the equal-transport system — the Salt and Iron Debate — after which the liquor monopoly was abolished. Corvée and taxes were lightened and the people rested, in the spirit of the Wen-Jing age. On the frontier, in the fourth Yuanfeng year, Fu Jiezi went to the Western Regions, slew the Loulan king Angui by stratagem, and renamed the state Shanshan, preserving the prestige of Han in that direction.

The court was not quiet. In the Shiyuan years the king of Yan plotted with Shangguan Jie, Sang Hongyang, and others to kill Huo Guang and depose the emperor; Zhao himself detected the forgery of the plot's letter. The affair failed, the plotters were executed with their clans, and Huo Guang came to dominate the court absolutely. The histories credit Zhao with early wisdom and a clear eye in judging cases, yet after the age of fourteen real power belonged entirely to Huo Guang; in his later years the emperor's figure recedes into the background of the regency.

In the fourth month of the first Yuanping year Emperor Zhao died at twenty-one, without issue. Huo Guang first summoned
; He was deposed after twenty-seven dissolute days, and Emperor Wu's great-grandson

was raised to the throne. The recuperative policies and regency structure accumulated in the Zhao reign continued as the Zhao-Xuan recovery, the last tranquil age of the Western Han's middle period.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hanshu*, ch. 7 (Benji of Emperor Zhao) and ch. 8 (Benji of Emperor Xuan); the biographies of Huo Guang, Fu Jiezi, and the Five Sons of Wu; the *Discourses on Salt and Iron*; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.summary_en: He succeeded after Emperor Zhao's death and was deposed after twenty-seven days for dissolute conduct; returned to his state, he was later enfeoffed as Marquis of Haihun.

timeline.title: 为昌邑王
timeline.summary: 李夫人孙，嗣昌邑王位。
timeline.summary_en: A grandson of Lady Li, he inherited the kingship of Changyi.

timeline.title: 迎立为帝
timeline.summary: 昭帝崩无嗣，霍光等迎贺即位。
timeline.summary_en: Emperor Zhao died without issue; Huo Guang and the others summoned He to the throne.

timeline.title: 淫戏无度
timeline.summary: 在位期间多过失，霍光等数其罪。
timeline.summary_en: In office he accumulated faults; Huo Guang and the others enumerated his crimes.

timeline.title: 被废
timeline.summary: 在位二十七日废，归昌邑，赐汤沐邑。
timeline.summary_en: He was deposed on his twenty-seventh day, sent back to Changyi, and given a stipend domain.

timeline.title: 废为海昏侯
timeline.summary: 宣帝时以罪削爵，封海昏侯。
timeline.summary_en: Under Emperor Xuan he was stripped of rank for fault and enfeoffed as Marquis of Haihun.

timeline.title: 短祚准帝
timeline.summary: 在位二十七日，图鉴作准帝短页。
timeline.summary_en: Twenty-seven days on the throne; the gazetteer lists him as quasi-emperor on a short page.

emperors.bio_md:
# 昌邑王贺 · 主要事迹

刘贺是[[han-wu-di|汉武帝]]之孙、昌邑哀王髆之子，袭昌邑王位。[[han-zhao-di|昭帝]]崩而无嗣，大将军霍光迎立昌邑王入继大统——这是西汉第一次「非先帝子而由大臣迎立」的皇位交接，而贺仅二十七日便以行淫乱被废，创下中国帝制史上最短的在位纪录之一。

从史书记载看，迎立之初即危机四伏：贺自昌邑率旧臣驰入长安，未及即位已露破绽；即位后不改藩国习气，肆意妄为。霍光遂与群臣会商，奏太后数其罪，废贺归国，赐汤沐邑二千户。霍光此举确立了「以太后名义废立皇帝」的先例，也把贺钉在了历史的耻辱柱上。

被废后的贺在昌邑过了十余年，宣帝[[han-xuan-di|汉宣帝]]时因故再削爵，封海昏侯，就国豫章（今江西）。他最终的归宿，是两千多年后南昌海昏侯墓的考古发现——数以万计的黄金、铜钱与简牍，让这位二十七日皇帝以另一种方式重新进入公众视野。图鉴以「准帝」立页，取其即位未及建元之实。

> 本地参考：点校本《汉书·霍光传》、《武五子传》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu He was a grandson of
, heir to the kingship of Changyi from his father, the lamented king Bo. When

died without issue, General-in-Chief Huo Guang summoned the king of Changyi to the throne — the first succession in which ministers rather than an heir brought in an outsider — and He was deposed after only twenty-seven days for dissolute conduct, setting one of the shortest reigns in Chinese imperial history.

From the histories, the accession was doomed from the start: He galloped into Chang'an with his Changyi partisans before he was even enthroned, and once on the throne he carried the habits of a feudatory court into the palace. Huo Guang convened the ministers, petitioned the empress dowager to enumerate his crimes, and had him deposed and sent back to Changyi with a stipend domain of two thousand households. The act established the precedent of deposing an emperor in the empress dowager's name — and fixed He on the historical pillory.

After his deposition He lived quietly in Changyi for over a decade, and under

he was further degraded and enfeoffed as Marquis of Haihun, to be settled in Yuzhang (present-day Jiangxi). His final fate was to re-enter public view two millennia later through the archaeology of the Haihun tomb near Nanchang — tens of thousands of gold pieces, coins, and bamboo slips making the twenty-seven-day emperor famous in a new way. This gazetteer lists him as a quasi-emperor, in view of a reign that never completed its first year.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hanshu*, biographies of Huo Guang and of the Five Sons of Emperor Wu; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.summary: 以皇曾孙之身自民间入继大统，亲政后综核名实、信赏必罚，置西域都护并受呼韩邪单于入朝的西汉中兴之主。
emperors.summary_en: Raised among the people as an imperial great-grandson, he succeeded to the throne, ruled by matching names to reality with sure rewards and punishments, established the Protector General of the Western Regions, and received Chanyu Huhanye at court, restoring Western Han.

portrait.appearance_basis: 史籍罕及形貌，传统画像符号化描写居多。MVP 用占位图；定稿前依时代冠服作艺术想象。

timeline.title: 民间长养
timeline.summary: 巫蛊之祸后皇曾孙病已养于民间，后入掖庭，经历底层与宫廷边缘。
timeline.summary_en: After the witchcraft affair, the imperial great-grandson Bingyi was raised among the people and later entered the palace wards, living at the bottom and the margins of the court.

timeline.title: 霍光迎立
timeline.summary: 昌邑王废后，霍光等迎立皇曾孙即位，是为宣帝。
timeline.summary_en: After the King of Changyi was deposed, Huo Guang and others installed the imperial great-grandson, who became Emperor Xuan.

timeline.title: 本始改元
timeline.summary: 改元本始，霍氏仍掌权，帝隐忍积蓄。
timeline.summary_en: The era changed to Benshi; the Huo clan still held power while the emperor bided his time and gathered strength.

timeline.title: 霍光薨逝
timeline.summary: 霍光死，宣帝逐步收回权柄，进入亲政前夜。
timeline.summary_en: With Huo Guang's death, Emperor Xuan gradually drew back authority, on the eve of personal rule.

timeline.title: 诛霍氏
timeline.summary: 霍禹等谋反事败，霍氏灭族，宣帝真正亲政，史称综核名实之始。
timeline.summary_en: Huo Yu's plot failed and the Huo clan was exterminated; Xuan truly ruled in person, called the beginning of matching names to reality.

timeline.title: 赵充国击羌
timeline.summary: 赵充国屯田破羌，西北边事为宣帝朝武功来源之一。
timeline.summary_en: Zhao Chongguo broke the Qiang through military agricultural colonies, one source of the reign's martial prestige on the northwestern frontier.

timeline.title: 西域都护
timeline.summary: 郑吉并护南北道，号都护，汉在西域制度化驻节。
timeline.summary_en: Zheng Ji guarded both the northern and southern routes as Protector General, institutionalizing Han's presence in the Western Regions.

timeline.title: 匈奴内乱与边策
timeline.summary: 匈奴内讧，汉廷边策调整，为呼韩邪来朝铺垫。
timeline.summary_en: Xiongnu infighting prompted the Han court to adjust frontier policy, paving the way for Huhanye's coming to court.

timeline.title: 呼韩邪朝汉
timeline.summary: 呼韩邪单于入朝称臣，匈汉关系进入新阶段，边事叙事高峰。
timeline.summary_en: Chanyu Huhanye came to court as a vassal, opening a new phase in Han-Xiongnu relations, the peak of the reign's frontier story.

timeline.title: 宣帝崩
timeline.summary: 宣帝崩，元帝即位；昭宣积累的吏治与边防格局转入下一朝。
timeline.summary_en: Xuan died and Emperor Yuan succeeded; the administrative and frontier order built under Zhao and Xuan passed to the next reign.

timeline.title: 信赏必罚吏治
timeline.summary: 察吏严明、循名责实，与武帝开边路径对照。
timeline.summary_en: Strict scrutiny of officials and holding reality to names, in contrast to Emperor Wu's expansionist path.

timeline.title: 综核名实
timeline.summary: 信赏必罚、察吏治、抑虚名，形成与武帝开边不同的收束型中兴路径。
timeline.summary_en: Sure rewards and punishments, disciplined officialdom, and suppressed empty fame formed a consolidative restoration, unlike Emperor Wu's expansion.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉宣帝 · 主要事迹

刘询以皇曾孙之身，在武帝末年的巫蛊之祸后养于民间、后入掖庭，从底层与宫廷边缘走入大统。这段早年经历使他「自民间来，知闾里奸邪、吏治得失」，成为理解其日后政风的钥匙。本页以《汉书·宣帝纪》为年表主线，辅以霍光、赵充国、郑吉、匈奴诸传与《资治通鉴》编年（本地参考库已备）。巫蛊之祸正是[[han-wu-di|汉武帝]]晚年宫廷震荡的余波，祖孙两朝可对读。

他的即位本身是权臣政治的峰值：元平元年昭帝崩、昌邑王废后，霍光等迎立皇曾孙。本始改元之初霍氏仍掌权，帝隐忍积蓄；地节二年霍光薨，宣帝逐步收回权柄；地节四年霍禹等谋反事败、霍氏灭族，宣帝方真正亲政。从迎立到族诛，八年之间完成了皇权对权臣的收束。

亲政之后的文治以「综核名实」为纲：信赏必罚、察吏严明、循名责实，形成与武帝开边不同的「收束型」中兴路径。「昭宣中兴」的评价口径历来不一，本图鉴取综核名实为主标签；霍光功过与宣帝权术，亦宜并读。

武功与边事则另有一条线：神爵元年赵充国屯田破羌，神爵二年郑吉并护南北道、号都护，汉廷在西域制度化驻节，是武帝开拓在宣帝朝的制度落点。五凤年间匈奴内讧，汉廷边策随之调整；甘露三年呼韩邪单于入朝称臣，匈汉关系进入新阶段，构成昭宣气象的边事高峰。

黄龙元年宣帝崩，元帝即位，昭宣积累的吏治与边防格局转入下一朝。与[[e-han-guangwu|汉光武帝]]对读：昭宣中兴与光武中兴，是重建帝国秩序的两条不同路径。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Bingyi, an imperial great-grandson, was raised among the people after the witchcraft affair of Emperor Wu's last years and later entered the palace wards, ascending from the bottom and the margins of the court to the throne. This early life, "come from among the people, knowing the wickedness of the alleys and the gains and losses of officialdom," is the key to his later style of rule. This page takes the "Annals of Emperor Xuan" in the Book of Han as its chronological spine, supplemented by the biographies of Huo Guang, Zhao Chongguo, Zheng Ji, and the Xiongnu, and by the chronicle of the Zizhi Tongjian (available in the local reference library). The witchcraft affair was itself the aftershock of the late-reign court turmoil of

, and the two reigns of great-grandfather and great-grandson can be read together.

His accession was itself the high-water mark of powerful-minister politics: in the first year of Yuanping, Emperor Zhao died, the King of Changyi was deposed, and Huo Guang and others installed the imperial great-grandson. At the start of the Benshi era the Huo clan still held power, and the emperor bided his time, husbanding his strength. In the second year of Dijie, Huo Guang died, and Xuan gradually drew back the reins; in the fourth year of Dijie, when Huo Yu's conspiracy failed and the Huo clan was exterminated, Xuan at last ruled in person. From enthronement to extermination, eight years completed the imperial house's reeling-in of the powerful minister.

His civil governance after assuming personal rule took "comprehensively checking names against reality" as its guiding principle: rewards were certain and punishments unfailing, officials were strictly examined, and reality was held accountable to names, forming a "consolidative" path of restoration distinct from Emperor Wu's expansion. Historical verdicts on the "Zhao-Xuan restoration" have never been uniform; this atlas takes the matching of names and reality as its primary label. Huo Guang's merits and faults, and Xuan's own political craft, are best read together.

War and frontier affairs form another thread: in the first year of Shenjue, Zhao Chongguo broke the Qiang through military agricultural colonies; in the second year, Zheng Ji combined the guardianship of the northern and southern routes under the title Protector General, and the Han court's institutionalized stationing in the Western Regions became the institutional resting point of Emperor Wu's expansion in Xuan's reign. During the Wufeng years the Xiongnu fell into civil strife, and Han frontier policy adjusted accordingly; in the third year of Ganlu, Chanyu Huhanye came to court as a vassal, opening a new phase in Han-Xiongnu relations and forming the frontier climax of the Zhao-Xuan era.

In the first year of Huanglong, Emperor Xuan died and Emperor Yuan succeeded; the administrative and frontier order accumulated under Zhao and Xuan passed into the next reign. Read alongside
: the Zhao-Xuan restoration and the Guangwu restoration are two different paths of rebuilding imperial order.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉元帝 · 主要事迹

刘奭是[[han-xuan-di|汉宣帝]]之子，立为太子时宣帝已有隐忧：太子柔仁好儒，宣帝曾叹「乱我家者太子也」。黄龙元年宣帝崩，奭即位，西汉由此从「霸王道杂之」的实干政治转向儒生政治——而这正是西汉由盛转衰的节点。

元帝朝开初尚有一番气象：征用贡禹等儒生，议罢甘泉、建章宫卫，减省用度；但政令渐成具文，优游不断成了元帝的痼疾。中书令石显乘机弄权，朝政壅蔽。武功方面，永光二年冯奉世击陇西羌，建昭三年甘延寿、陈汤矫制发兵，斩郅支单于于康居——「明犯强汉者，虽远必诛」的豪语即出于此役，然皆臣下之力，帝无所与。

竟宁元年，呼韩邪单于入朝请婚，元帝以后宫良家子王昭君赐之，昭君出塞成为汉匈和亲的最后华章。同年五月，元帝崩，[[han-cheng-di|成帝]]即位。史称元帝「牵制文义，优游不断」，元成之世，外戚与宦官问题相继累积，汉室之衰自此而始。

> 本地参考：点校本《汉书》卷009《元帝纪》、卷094《匈奴传》，《贡禹传》、《陈汤传》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Shi was the son of

. Even when Shi was made heir apparent, Xuan had misgivings: the heir was gentle and devoted to Confucian learning, and Xuan once sighed that "the one who will throw my house into disorder is the heir apparent." When Xuan died in the first Huanglong year, Shi succeeded, and Western Han turned from the pragmatic "mixed way of king and hegemon" to Confucian politics — the hinge of the dynasty's decline.

His reign opened with some promise: Confucian scholars such as Gong Yu were summoned, and the garrisons of the Ganquan and Jianzhang palaces were debated and trimmed. But the edicts dissolved into formalism, and irresolution became Yuan's chronic ailment; Shi Xian, chief of the Inner Secretariat, seized power and clogged the court. On the frontier, Feng Fengshi crushed a Qiang revolt in Longxi in the second Yongguang year, and in the third Jianzhao year Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang, acting on their own authority, slew the Zhizhi chanyu in Kangju — the boast "whoever offends mighty Han shall be punished, however distant" dates from that campaign — yet all was the work of ministers, with the emperor having no part.

In the first Jingning year the Huhanye chanyu came to court seeking a bride, and Yuan granted him the palace woman Wang Zhaojun; her departure became the last great chapter of Han-Xiongnu marriage alliance. In the fifth month of the same year, Yuan died and

succeeded. The historians wrote that Yuan was "fettered by the letter of the classics, irresolute to the end"; in the Yuan-Cheng age, consort-clan and eunuch problems accumulated in turn, and the decline of the house of Han began here.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hanshu*, ch. 9 (Benji of Emperor Yuan), ch. 94 (Treatise on the Xiongnu), and the biographies of Gong Yu and Chen Tang; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉成帝 · 主要事迹

刘骜是[[han-yuan-di|汉元帝]]太子，生于甲观画堂，本以太孙之尊承统。然成帝一朝的政治轨迹，却是西汉外戚问题最典型的样本：即位次年即封诸舅，王氏兄弟子侄布满朝堂，王凤、王商、王音、王根相继执政，「王氏一日五侯」自此始。

成帝本人湛于酒色，朝政委于母族：河平元年黄河决于东郡，朝廷治河备至；鸿嘉永始间营建昌陵，功费巨万，终以罢昌陵还复延陵收场。后宫之变尤烈——鸿嘉三年许皇后废，永始元年立赵飞燕为后，赵氏姐妹专宠十余年，而帝竟无嗣。绥和元年，立定陶王刘欣为太子，即后来的[[han-ai-di|哀帝]]。

绥和二年，王根荐其侄王莽为大司马，王氏之权达到顶点；三月，成帝暴崩，年四十五。史臣评曰「湛于酒色，赵氏乱内，外家擅朝」——成帝朝二十六年，汉家政权结构的肿瘤已经长成：外戚擅朝、后宫乱政、储位难定，而[[xin-wang-mang|王莽]]正是从王氏外戚的土壤里长出来的。西汉之亡，其伏笔大半种于成帝之世。

> 本地参考：点校本《汉书》卷010《成帝纪》、《元后传》、《外戚传》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Ao, heir of

, was born in the Jiaguan painted hall and came to the throne with every expectation of the empire's crown prince. Yet the politics of his reign became the classic specimen of Western Han's consort-clan disease: in the first year after accession he enfeoffed his maternal uncles, and the Wang brothers and nephews filled the court — Wang Feng, Wang Shang, Wang Yin, and Wang Gen governing in turn, with "five Wang marquises in a single day" as the byword of the age.

Cheng himself was sunk in wine and women, leaving government to his mother's family: in the first Heping year the Yellow River broke at Dongjun, making river control a great matter of state; in the Hongjia-Yongshi years the Changling mausoleum project consumed enormous resources before being abandoned in favor of Yanling; and in the harem the crises ran deeper — Empress Xu was deposed in the third Hongjia year, and in the first Yongshi year Zhao Feiyan was made empress, the Zhao sisters monopolizing favor for a decade while the emperor produced no heir. In the first Suihe year he made Liu Xin, king of Dingtao, heir apparent — the future

.

In the second Suihe year, Wang Gen recommended his nephew Wang Mang as Grand Commander-in-Chief, carrying Wang power to its peak; in the third month Cheng died suddenly at forty-five. The historians' verdict: "sunk in wine and women; the Zhaos threw the inner court into disorder; the maternal kin ran the government." In twenty-six years the tumor in the structure of the Han state grew complete — consort power, harem intrigue, and a throne without an heir — and

grew from exactly that soil. The fall of Western Han was largely seeded in the reign of Cheng.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hanshu*, ch. 10 (Benji of Emperor Cheng), the biography of Empress Yuan, and the biography of the Consorts; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). emperors.bio_md:
# 汉哀帝 · 主要事迹

刘欣是[[han-cheng-di|成帝]]的养子，本为定陶王，绥和元年入继为太子，次年成帝暴崩，即位。哀帝年少而欲有为，一上台就想革除王氏外戚把持朝政的积弊——然而六年之间，改革尽成泡影，汉家国祚反而加速滑向王莽。

哀帝朝的大事，件件指向「强主威」而件件落空：即位初诏议限田限奴婢，师丹等议之而卒不行，贵族豪强的反弹使限田令胎死腹中；建平二年听信夏贺良等改元易号，闹出「陈圣刘太平皇帝」的笑话，旋又自罢；为压王氏之势，他扶植祖母傅氏、母亲丁氏一族与董贤，结果董贤宠极人臣，「断袖」之宠名传千古，而主威愈弱。

元寿二年，乌珠留单于入朝，是西汉末年少有的一次四夷来朝的体面场面；同年六月，哀帝崩，无子。太皇太后王政君即日收回玺绶，召[[xin-wang-mang|王莽]]入宫，董贤自杀。史赞谓哀帝「睹孝成之世，禄去公室，欲强主威，而丁、傅、董贤乱之」——他不是没有振作的念头，只是西汉的制度病已入膏肓，非一君之力所能救。

> 本地参考：点校本《汉书》卷011《哀帝纪》、《佞幸传》、《食货志》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Xin, the adopted heir of

, had been king of Dingtao; he entered the succession in the first Suihe year and took the throne when Cheng died the next year. Young and eager to act, he meant from the start to break the grip of the Wang consorts on the government — yet in six years every reform came to nothing, and the Han mandate slid faster toward Wang Mang.

Each great matter of his reign aimed at "strengthening the sovereign" and each failed: on accession he ordered a debate on limiting fields and slaves; Shi Dan's proposals died in the face of aristocratic opposition. In the second Jianping year he let Xia Heliang and others persuade him to change era and title, producing the farce of "the Chengsheng Liu Taiping emperor," soon rescinded. To counter the Wangs he raised his grandmother's Fu clan, his mother's Ding clan, and above all Dong Xian — whose favor exceeded all precedent, the "severed sleeve" infatuation passing into proverb, while the throne's authority only weakened.

In the second Yuanshou year the Wuzhuliu chanyu came to court, one of the last dignified scenes of four-tribes homage in Western Han; in the sixth month of that year Ai died without issue. The grand empress dowager Wang Zhengjun took back the seal the same day, summoned

into the palace, and Dong Xian killed himself. The historians' eulogy: "Having seen in the reign of Cheng the offices drained from the royal house, he wished to strengthen the sovereign's authority — but the Dings, the Fus, and Dong Xian disordered it." He was not without the will to reform; the institutional disease of Western Han was simply past cure by any single ruler.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hanshu*, ch. 11 (Benji of Emperor Ai), the biography of the Favorites, and the Treatise on Food and Money; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). emperors.bio_md:
# 汉平帝 · 主要事迹

刘衎是中山孝王刘兴之子，生于中山。元寿二年[[han-ai-di|哀帝]]崩而无嗣，太皇太后王政君与[[xin-wang-mang|王莽]]定策，迎九岁的刘衎入长安即位，是为平帝。他即位的那一天起，「政由莽出」就写在了西汉最后一份年号的每一个字里。

元始年间看似文治斐然，实则全部是王莽的表演：元年废成帝赵皇后、哀帝傅皇后，莽为安汉公；二年莽女配帝，立为皇后；三年为学者筑舍万区，立官稷、学官，郡国乡聚皆置学官；四年加宰衡，上公之位；同年群臣奏请九锡，莽受之——安汉公、宰衡、九锡，篡汉的仪式一步步走完，每走一步，平帝的本纪就多一行干巴巴的系年。

元始五年十二月，平帝崩，年十四。本纪只书「崩」字；《王莽传》则载莽以毒酒进帝之说——两说并存，史不能决。帝崩后，莽立宣帝玄孙刘婴为皇太子，号孺子，居摄践祚，两年后即取汉而代之。平帝本纪虽存，军国大事无出其手，他是西汉帝系上最彻底的傀儡：九岁入继，十四岁暴崩，中间五年，全是别人替他写好的剧本。

> 本地参考：点校本《汉书》卷012《平帝纪》、卷099《王莽传》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Kan was the son of Liu Xing, the filial king of Zhongshan, born in Zhongshan. When
died without issue in the second Yuanshou year, the grand empress dowager Wang Zhengjun and

settled on him, and the nine-year-old king of Zhongshan was brought to Chang'an as Emperor Ping. From his first day "all policy came from Mang," written into every character of the last era name of Western Han.

The Yuanshi years looked like an age of flourishing culture, but every flourish was Wang Mang's theater: in the first year, the Zhao empress dowager of Cheng and the Fu empress dowager of Ai were deposed, and Mang took the title "Duke Who Settles Han"; in the second, Mang's daughter married the emperor and was made empress; in the third, ten thousand quarters were built for scholars, with state altars and schools established through every commandery and district; in the fourth Mang took the title "Chief of the Realm," above the Three Dukes, and the ministers petitioned the Nine Distinctions, which he accepted — Duke Who Settles Han, Chief of the Realm, Nine Distinctions: the ceremonial steps of usurpation completed one by one, each step adding one dry line of dating to Ping's annals.

In the twelfth month of the fifth Yuanshi year Ping died at fourteen. The benji records only the word "died"; the Wang Mang biography carries the tale of poisoned wine. The two versions stand together, and history cannot decide. After his death Mang raised Xuan's great-great-grandson Ying as heir, styled "the Infant," took the regency, and two years later took the dynasty itself. Ping's annals survive, but no matter of state passed through his hands: he was the most complete puppet on the Western Han throne — brought in at nine, dead at fourteen, the five years between being a script written entirely by others.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hanshu*, ch. 12 (Benji of Emperor Ping) and ch. 99 (Biography of Wang Mang); Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 孺子婴 · 主要事迹

刘婴是宣帝玄孙，[[han-ping-di|平帝]]崩后，[[xin-wang-mang|王莽]]立年仅二岁的刘婴为皇太子，号「孺子」，自己以周公自居，居摄践祚，称「假皇帝」——西汉名义上的最后一个皇帝，连正式即位都没有，便成了禅让大戏的道具。

居摄三年间，反对者并未绝迹：居摄二年，东郡太守翟义起兵讨莽，声势震动关东，旋被讨平。莽一面以武力镇压，一面加紧造势——初始元年，符命祥瑞与劝进表章如雪片般飞向长安，王莽终于在始建国元年废孺子为定安公，称帝改国号为新，西汉至此正式灭亡。

被废后的刘婴被幽闭禁锢，年岁渐长却不通人语；更始年间天下大乱，婴死于乱兵。他是中国帝制史上最年幼、最彻底的傀儡之一：两岁受命，四岁失国，一生从未真正拥有过任何权力，却偏偏以「皇帝」之名被写进史书。图鉴以「准帝」立页，附于王莽禅代与[[e-han-guangwu|光武中兴]]两端之间，正可作汉祚兴亡的注脚。

> 本地参考：点校本《汉书》卷099《王莽传》、《后汉书·刘玄传》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

立年仅二岁的刘婴为皇太子，号「孺子」，自己以周公自居，居摄践祚，称「假皇帝」——西汉名义上的最后一个皇帝，连正式即位都没有，便成了禅让大戏的道具。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Ying was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Xuan. After
died,

raised the two-year-old Ying as heir apparent, styled "the Infant," casting himself as the Duke of Zhou and taking the regency in the infant's place, calling himself "Acting Emperor" — the nominal last emperor of Western Han, who was never even formally enthroned, became the prop of an abdication drama.

The three regency years were not without opposition: in the second Jushe year, Zhai Yi, governor of Dongjun, rose against Mang with an army that shook the lands east of the passes before being suppressed. Mang answered force with force and momentum with theater — in the first Chushi year, omens and petitions urging abdication flew into Chang'an like snow; in the first Shijianguo year he demoted the Infant to Duke of Ding'an, proclaimed himself emperor, and changed the dynasty's name to Xin. Western Han was formally finished.

The deposed Infant was shut away, and as he grew he could not even speak coherently; during the Gengshi era, amid the collapse of the Xin dynasty, he died in the disorder of the soldiery. He is among the youngest and most complete puppets in Chinese imperial history: invested at two, losing the state at four, never holding a scrap of power, yet written into the histories under the title of emperor. This gazetteer lists him as a quasi-emperor, standing between Mang's usurpation and the restoration of

— a footnote to the rise and fall of the Han mandate.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hanshu*, ch. 99 (Biography of Wang Mang), and the *Hou Hanshu*, biography of Liu Xuan; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 新朝王莽 · 主要事迹

王莽是两汉之际几乎绕不开的枢纽人物：他以外戚身份登上权力顶峰，亲手终结西汉，又以一场托古改制把新朝推向速亡。本页以《汉书·王莽传》为年表主线，辅以《后汉书·光武帝纪》与《资治通鉴》编年（本地参考库已备）。

他的上升路径以儒入局。姑母王政君为汉元帝皇后，王莽凭外戚身份与儒学声望累迁，元始年间受封安汉公、掌控朝政。平帝死后，他立孺子婴而居摄，行周公故事，加号假皇帝；初始元年符命、禅让舆论密集，为代汉铺平合法性。始建国元年（公元9年），他废孺子婴，建国号新。

称帝之后，他托《周礼》等经典力行改制：行王田、禁奴婢，屡改货币与官名，又设五均六筦加深经济管制，社会震荡剧烈；对外与匈奴关系破裂，边费与兵祸并起。制度蓝图的气象与现实承受的代价之间，裂缝迅速扩大。

天凤年间，绿林、赤眉等民变蜂起，新朝控制力崩解；地皇三年荆州绿林大起，地方失控。地皇四年，新军大败于昆阳，更始政权随即进逼，长安陷落，王莽死于渐台，新朝十四年而亡。

与[[e-han-guangwu|汉光武帝]]对读：一人以符命禅让取天下而骤亡，一人于昆阳兴起而重建汉室。王莽的评价长期在「篡贼」与「理想主义改革者」两极之间摆动；本项目月旦取负，但其改制的讨论价值仍留待后效。

bio_parts_en.value:
Wang Mang is a pivotal figure that no account of the interlude between the two Han dynasties can bypass: he climbed to the summit of power as a consort-clan kinsman, ended Western Han with his own hands, and then drove his Xin dynasty to swift ruin through a program of archaizing reform. This page takes the "Biography of Wang Mang" in the Book of Han as its chronological spine, supplemented by the "Annals of Emperor Guangwu" in the Book of the Later Han and the chronicle of the Zizhi Tongjian (available in the local reference library).

His rise entered through the Confucian gate. His aunt Wang Zhengjun was Emperor Yuan's empress; on the strength of his consort-clan standing and Confucian renown he rose step by step, being enfeoffed Duke of Anhan during the Yuanshi years and taking control of the court. After Emperor Ping's death he set up the infant Ruzi Ying and acted as regent, reenacting the precedent of the Duke of Zhou and adding the title Acting Emperor. In the first year of Chushi, portents and abdication propaganda crowded thick, smoothing the legitimacy of replacing Han. In the first year of Shijianguo (AD 9), he deposed Ruzi Ying and founded a dynasty named Xin.

Once emperor, he pressed reforms on the authority of the Rites of Zhou and other classics: he instituted "king's fields" and banned the trade in slaves, repeatedly changed the coinage and the names of offices, and deepened economic regimentation through the Five Equalizations and Six Monopolies, shaking society violently. Abroad, relations with the Xiongnu broke down, and frontier costs rose together with the ravages of war. The crack between the grandeur of the institutional blueprint and the price reality had to pay widened fast.

During the Tianfeng years, popular revolts, the Lulin, the Red Eyebrows, and others, swarmed up, and Xin's grip disintegrated; in the third year of Dihuang the Lulin forces in Jingzhou rose in strength, and local control was lost. In the fourth year of Dihuang, the Xin army was crushed at Kunyang; the Gengshi regime pressed in at once, Chang'an fell, Wang Mang died on the Jian Terrace, and Xin perished after fourteen years.

Read alongside

: one took the realm through portents and abdication and perished abruptly; the other rose at Kunyang and rebuilt the Han house. Verdicts on Wang Mang have long swung between the poles of "usurping traitor" and "idealist reformer"; this project's judgment is negative, but the value of debating his reforms is left to the future.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉光武帝 · 主要事迹

刘秀是新末乱世中重建汉室的中兴之主。本页以《后汉书·光武帝纪》为年表主线，辅以云台诸将与马援诸传互见（本地参考库已备）。

新莽地皇三年（22），他随宗室宾客起兵于舂陵，卷入反新浪潮；次年昆阳之战以少击众，大破[[xin-wang-mang|王莽]]新军主力，一举奠定军事声望。更始年间，他渡河经营河北，收揽人才，与更始政权渐行渐远；建武元年（25）于鄗南即皇帝位，建元建武，国号续汉，随即定都洛阳，东汉政治中心由此确立。

建国之后，他一面收束武功，一面塑造政风。建武二年大封功臣，云台班底成形；建武十二年平公孙述等，全国粗定，中兴局面落定；建武十九年，马援等平交趾，武功延伸至南疆。文治一面，他崇尚柔道、退功臣进文吏，不使功臣揽政；建武十五年推行度田，检核田亩户口，曾引发地方反抗与政策调整，成为其治世中争议最集中的节点。

晚年，他于中元元年（56）封禅泰山，中兴礼仪达于高峰，可与[[han-wu-di|汉武帝]]的封禅对读：一人把统一帝国的武功与礼仪推向极盛，一人在废墟之后以此告成功于天地。翌年（中元二年，57）他崩于洛阳，明帝继位，东汉国祚得以延续。史家评点多聚焦于「柔道」与度田之争，总体月旦正面。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Xiu was the restoration sovereign who rebuilt the Han house amid the chaos at the end of the Xin dynasty. This page takes the 《后汉书·光武帝纪》 as its chronological backbone, cross-referenced with the biographies of the Yuntai generals and of Ma Yuan (available in the local reference library).

In Dihuang 3 of the Xin (22), he rose in arms at Chongling with imperial kinsmen and retainers, joining the tide of revolt against the Xin; the next year, at the Battle of Kunyang, he struck the many with the few and shattered the main Xin army of

, establishing his military renown in a single stroke. During the Gengshi period he crossed the river to build a base in Hebei, gathering talent and drifting steadily away from the Gengshi regime; in Jianwu 1 (25) he took the imperial throne south of Hao, founded the Jianwu era, continued the Han dynastic name, and soon fixed the capital at Luoyang, thereby establishing the political center of the Eastern Han.

Once the state was founded, he wound down military ventures while shaping the political climate. In Jianwu 2 he broadly enfeoffed meritorious officials, and the Yuntai cohort took shape; in Jianwu 12 he defeated Gongsun Shu and other rivals, the realm was roughly pacified, and the restoration settled into place; in Jianwu 19 Ma Yuan and others pacified Jiaozhi, extending the martial record to the southern frontier. On the civil side, he prized the "way of softness," retired meritorious generals in favor of civil officials, and kept the generals from holding power; in Jianwu 15 he pushed through the land survey, auditing fields and households, which provoked local resistance and policy adjustments — the most contested node of his rule.

In his later years, in Zhongyuan 1 (56), he performed the Feng and Shan sacrifices at Mount Tai, the ritual high point of the restoration, which can be read against the Feng-Shan of

: one carried the unified empire's martial and ritual order to its zenith, the other used the same rites to announce to Heaven and Earth that success had been won from ruins. The following year (Zhongyuan 2, 57) he died at Luoyang; Emperor Ming succeeded him, and the Eastern Han dynastic line was preserved. Historians' verdicts focus on the "way of softness" and the land-survey controversy, and are on the whole favorable.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉明帝 · 主要事迹

刘庄是[[e-han-guangwu|汉光武帝]]第四子，母阴皇后。光武建武十九年，郭后废、阴后立，庄得为皇太子，师事桓荣习《尚书》。中元二年光武崩，庄即位，年三十——他接手的是一个刚完成统一的帝国，而他给这个帝国定下的主调是「严切」。

明帝治国以法纪为纲：后宫之家不得封侯与政，馆陶公主为子求郎，明帝不许而赐钱千万；楚王英之狱牵连甚广，虽云过苛，亦见其不徇亲贵。永平年间，北郊礼乐、冠冕车服诸制度次第厘定；永平中图画云台二十八将，追感创业功臣；永平八年诏报楚王英助「伊蒲塞桑门」之盛馔，是官方文书较早涉及浮屠者，佛教之入华，于此可见端绪。永平十二年遣王景修汴渠，自荥阳至千乘海口，河汴分流，为东汉最大水利工程。

武功方面，永平十六年窦固伐北匈奴，取伊吾卢地，置宜禾都尉；同年班超与郭恂俱使西域，次年击车师，西域诸国复遣子入侍——东汉对西域的经营，由明帝一朝奠定格局。永平十八年八月，明帝崩于东宫前殿，年四十八，遗诏无起寝庙。他留给[[e-han-zhang|章帝]]的，是一个法令分明、内外俱治的朝廷；明章之治并称，正以此故。

> 本地参考：点校本《后汉书》卷002《显宗孝明帝纪》、《班超传》、《王景传》、《楚王英传》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Zhuang was the fourth son of

, by Empress Yin. In the nineteenth Jianwu year, with Empress Guo deposed and Yin raised in her place, Zhuang became heir apparent, studying the *Documents* under Huan Rong. When Guangwu died in the second Zhongyuan year, Zhuang took the throne at thirty — inheriting an empire just reunited, to which he gave the keynote of strict discipline.

He governed by law and regulation: no family of the inner palace might be enfeoffed or take part in government; when Princess Guantao asked an office for her son, Ming refused and gave her ten million cash instead. The case of Prince Ying of Chu drew a wide net — harsh, perhaps, but proof that he would not spare the favored. In the Yongping years the Northern Suburb rites, caps, and carriage regalia were settled one by one; in mid-Yongping the Twenty-eight Generals were painted in the Yuntai Hall in memory of the founders; and in the eighth Yongping year an edict answered Prince Ying's patronage of "upasaka and shramana" feasts — among the earliest mentions of Buddhism in official documents, a first trace of the Dharma's entry into China. In the twelfth Yongping year Wang Jing was sent to repair the Bian canal from Xingyang to the Qiansheng estuary, separating river and canal — the greatest water project of Eastern Han.

In the sixteenth Yongping year Dou Gu struck the northern Xiongnu and took the Yiwulu lands, installing the Yihe commandant; in the same year Ban Chao and Guo Xun were sent to the Western Regions, and the next year Cheshi was taken and the states of the Western Regions again sent sons to serve at court — the Eastern Han's opening of the west was settled in Ming's reign. In the eighth month of the eighteenth Yongping year he died in the front hall of the Eastern Palace at forty-eight, his will ordering no memorial temple. What he left

was a court where law was clear and affairs in order; the paired fame of the Ming-Zhang age rests on exactly this.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 2 (Benji of Emperor Ming), and the biographies of Ban Chao, Wang Jing, and Prince Ying of Chu; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉章帝 · 主要事迹

刘炟是[[e-han-ming|汉明帝]]之子，永平三年立为皇太子，永平十八年即位，在位十三年。他承光武、明帝两朝之余烈，政风一转而尚宽厚，《后汉书》论曰「事从宽厚」，史家遂以「长者」目之；明章两代与光武朝并称东汉初年的治世。

章帝朝的文化大事是建初四年的白虎观会议：诸儒讲论五经同异，章帝亲称制临决，其后班固等撰集为《白虎通义》，今文经学由此定于一尊。政事方面，他宽刑省罚、劝农恤民，灾异之后诏举贤良；元和年间两度出巡，南至南阳，北至河内，行籍田之礼。边事则承明帝余威，章和元年班超击破焉耆，西域诸国复归汉家版图。

宽厚的一面也有其代价：建初三年立窦氏为皇后，窦氏一门渐受宠任，马防击羌、班超定西域之际，外戚已隐然成势。章帝晚年对此并非无觉，然终未能裁抑。章和二年章帝崩，和帝年仅十岁，窦太后临朝，窦宪兄弟擅权，外戚专权从此成为东汉政治的顽疾。

章帝与[[e-han-guangwu|汉光武帝]]、明帝并观，正可见东汉由创业而守文的路径：光武以柔道安邦，明帝以严切整饬，章帝则以宽厚守成——成就了明章之治，也把外戚问题的引信留给了后继者。

> 本地参考：点校本《后汉书》卷003《肃宗孝章帝纪》、卷002《明帝纪》、卷004《和帝纪》，《班固传》、《班超传》、《皇后纪》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Da was the son of

. Made heir apparent in the third Yongping year, he succeeded in the eighteenth and reigned thirteen years. Inheriting the accumulated strength of the reigns of Guangwu and Ming, he turned the tone of government toward breadth and lenience; the *Hou Hanshu* records that "his rule was broad and lenient," and the historians called him "the elder-sage." The reigns of Ming and Zhang, with that of Guangwu, together form the golden age of early Eastern Han.

The cultural landmark of his reign was the White Tiger Hall Conference in the fourth Jianchu year: the scholars debated the agreements and differences of the Five Classics, the emperor pronounced the final verdict in person, and Ban Gu and others compiled the results as the *Baihu tongyi*, fixing the supremacy of the New-Text school. In administration he lightened punishments, encouraged farming, and relieved the people, summoning worthy men after earthquakes and other portents; in the Yuanhe years he made two progresses, south to Nanyang and north to Henei, performing the rite of ploughing the sacred field. On the frontier, carrying on the prestige of Ming's reign, Ban Chao broke Yanqi in the first Zhanghe year, and the states of the Western Regions returned to the Han map.

The lenient side had its price: in the third Jianchu year Dou was made empress, and the Dou clan grew in favor; by the time of Ma Fang's Qiang campaigns and Ban Chao's conquests, the consort families were already gathering strength. Zhang was not unaware of this in his later years, but he could never trim them. When he died in the second Zhanghe year, Emperor He was only ten; Empress Dowager Dou took the regency, and the Dou brothers dominated the government — consort-clan autocracy, from then on, became the chronic illness of Eastern Han politics.

Seen beside

and Emperor Ming, Zhang traces the path of Eastern Han from founding to consolidation: Guangwu settled the realm by the soft way, Ming disciplined it with strictness, and Zhang maintained it with lenience — achieving the Ming-Zhang age while handing the fuse of the consort-clan question to his successors.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 3 (Benji of Emperor Zhang), ch. 2 (Emperor Ming), and ch. 4 (Emperor He); the biographies of Ban Gu, Ban Chao, and the Annals of the Empresses; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉和帝 · 主要事迹

刘肇是[[e-han-zhang|章帝]]之子，章和二年即位，年十岁，窦太后临朝，窦宪兄弟秉权。这是东汉幼主政治的开端：从此以后，外戚临朝、宦官预政、皇帝冲龄，成了东汉中后期政局的三重奏。

和帝朝的大事有二。其一是武功：永元元年，窦宪大破北匈奴，登燕然山刻石勒功，班固作《封燕然山铭》；永元三年，北单于远遁，北匈奴自此西迁，在中国史籍中淡出——这是汉匈战争史上最后一个大场面，而其主帅窦宪正是一个野心勃勃的外戚。其二是收权：永元四年，年仅十四岁的和帝与宦官郑众定计，收窦宪大将军印绶，窦氏诸兄弟皆自杀，外戚之祸暂告平息。然而代价随之而来：郑众封鄛乡侯，宦官封侯用权自此始。

亲政之后，和帝遵奉明章故事，永元九年蝗灾，诏举有道、求言恤民；班超经营西域，永元六年定焉耆，西域五十余国悉纳质内属，永元十四年班超年老还洛，次年病卒。元兴元年，和帝崩，年二十七。史称永元之政「遵奉故事，未有阙失」，然幼主之世，外戚与宦官已然交替登场——和帝亲政的十四年，正是东汉由盛转衰的过渡带。

> 本地参考：点校本《后汉书》卷004《孝和帝纪》、《窦宪传》、《班超传》、《宦者传》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Zhao was the son of

. He took the throne in the second Zhanghe year at ten, with Empress Dowager Dou in the regency and Dou Xian and his brothers in power. This was the beginning of Eastern Han's child-emperor politics: from then on, consort regencies, eunuch meddling, and infant sovereigns formed the three-part theme of the dynasty's middle and late periods.

Two great matters mark his reign. The first was military: in the first Yongyuan year Dou Xian broke the northern Xiongnu and carved a commemoration on Mount Yanran, for which Ban Gu composed the "Yanran Mountain Inscription"; in the third Yongyuan year the northern chanyu fled far away, and the northern Xiongnu began their westward migration, fading from the Chinese records — the last great scene of the Han-Xiongnu wars, commanded by an ambitious consort. The second was the recovery of power: in the fourth Yongyuan year the fourteen-year-old emperor plotted with the eunuch Zheng Zhong, seized Dou Xian's seal of office, and the Dou brothers all died; the consort scourge was briefly laid. But the price came at once: Zheng Zhong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chaoxiang, and the rise of enfeoffed, powerful eunuchs began here.

After taking power he followed the Ming-Zhang precedents: in the ninth Yongyuan year locusts struck, and he summoned the worthy and sought counsel for the people; Ban Chao's work in the Western Regions culminated in the sixth Yongyuan year with the submission of Yanqi, the states of the west sending hostages to court, and in the fourteenth Yongyuan year the aging Ban Chao returned to Luoyang, dying the next year. In the first Yuanxing year Emperor He died at twenty-seven. The historians say the Yongyuan government "followed the established precedents without lapse," yet in an age of child emperors the consorts and eunuchs had already begun their alternation — the fourteen years of He's personal rule were the transition zone of Eastern Han's decline.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 4 (Benji of Emperor He), and the biographies of Dou Xian, Ban Chao, and the Eunuchs; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉殇帝 · 主要事迹

刘隆是[[e-han-he|和帝]]少子。元兴元年十二月，和帝崩，皇后邓绥迎立尚在襁褓的刘隆为帝——即位时出生不过百余日，是中国帝制史上即位年龄最小的皇帝。

殇帝在位不足一年，朝政自始便在邓绥的临朝称制之下：邓后以女主之身摄政，尚能以宽简为治，史载延平年间政令颇有可观者，然皆其祖母所为，与这个百天之帝无关。延平元年八月，殇帝崩，在位不满周岁，葬康陵。

殇帝之立与殇帝之崩，是东汉幼主政治的第一个极端样本：皇帝已经幼小到无法成为任何意义上的政治主体，皇权只是太后与外戚手中的一个名号。邓后旋定策迎立清河王子[[e-han-an|刘祜]]，是为安帝——东汉的每一次权力交接，从此都要经过宫闱之内的定策。

> 本地参考：点校本《后汉书》卷004《孝殇帝纪》、《皇后纪·和熹邓皇后》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Long was the youngest son of

. In the twelfth month of the first Yuanxing year, Emperor He died, and Empress Deng Sui brought in the infant Liu Long as emperor — barely a hundred days old at his accession, the youngest emperor ever enthroned in Chinese imperial history.

He reigned less than a year, and government was from the start in the hands of Deng Sui's regency: the empress dowager ruled as a woman in her own right, and the histories credit the Yanping years with a measure of lenient order — all her doing, nothing to do with the hundred-day emperor. In the eighth month of Yanping 1 he died, having reigned under a year, and was buried at Kangling.

His enthronement and his death are the first extreme specimen of Eastern Han's child-emperor politics: the sovereign had become too young to be any kind of political subject, and imperial power was merely a title in the hands of an empress dowager and her kin. Deng then chose Hu, son of the prince of Qinghe, as

— from then on, every succession in Eastern Han passed through a decision made behind the palace gates.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 4 (Benji of Emperor Shang) and the Annals of the Empresses (Empress Deng); Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉安帝 · 主要事迹

刘祜是清河孝王刘庆之子。延平元年[[e-han-shang|殇帝]]崩，邓太后与兄邓骘定策禁中，迎立年十三的刘祜，是为安帝。他的前十五年，是邓后临朝的十五年：永初年间的政令多出邓氏，安帝本人不过系年而已。

安帝朝最大的问题是边患。永初元年，西域诸国叛汉，汉罢都护；永初二年，先零羌大叛，凉州残破，汉连年发兵征讨，国用为之空竭，「永初羌乱」耗尽了东汉前期的积蓄。朝中甚至有弃凉州之议，赖虞诩力驳而止。邓后主政期间尚能维持局面，建光元年邓后崩，安帝始得亲政，却立刻诛邓骘等邓氏诸人，转而信用乳母王圣与宦官江京、樊丰等，朝政愈趋壅蔽。

延光三年，安帝废皇太子刘保为济阴王——这个决定为十年后宦官拥立[[e-han-shun|顺帝]]埋下伏笔。延光四年，安帝南巡，崩于叶县，年三十二。阎皇后秘不发丧，与江京等定策立北乡侯[[e-han-shao-bei|刘懿]]，翌年北乡侯薨，宦官孙程等十九人迎立济阴王，东汉由此进入宦官与外戚交替废立的中晚期。史论谓安帝「虽称尊享祀，而令德不终」，其亲政数年，正是东汉政局全面恶化的开始。

> 本地参考：点校本《后汉书》卷005《孝安帝纪》、《西羌传》、《虞诩传》、《皇后纪》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Hu was the son of the filial king Qing of Qinghe. In the first Yanping year, after the death of

, Empress Dowager Deng and her brother Deng Zhi decided behind closed doors to raise the thirteen-year-old Hu as Emperor An. His first fifteen years were the fifteen years of the Deng regency: the Yongchu edicts issued from the Deng house, and An himself was no more than a date in the annals.

His reign's gravest problem was the frontier. In the first Yongchu year the states of the Western Regions turned against Han and the protectorate was abolished; in the second Yongchu year the Xianling Qiang rose in force, Liangzhou was devastated, and year after year troops were raised until the treasury was empty — the "Yongchu Qiang wars" exhausted the accumulated strength of early Eastern Han. There was even a proposal to abandon Liangzhou, rejected only by the arguments of Yu Xu. The Deng regency could still hold the line; but in the first Jianguang year Empress Dowager Deng died, and An, at last ruling in person, at once destroyed Deng Zhi and the Deng house, turning instead to his wet nurse Wang Sheng and the eunuchs Jiang Jing and Fan Feng — the court grew more obstructed than ever.

In the third Yanguang year he deposed Crown Prince Bao as prince of Jiyin — a decision that planted the seed of the eunuch enthronement of

a decade later. In the fourth Yanguang year An died at Ye during a southern tour, aged thirty-two. Empress Yan concealed the death, and with Jiang Jing and others raised the Marquis of Beixiang; when the marquis died the next year, the eunuch Sun Cheng and nineteen others enthroned the prince of Jiyin, and Eastern Han entered its middle-late phase of alternating eunuch and consort usurpation. The historians said of An that "though he sat on the throne and received sacrifice, his good name did not end well"; his years of personal rule mark the beginning of the dynasty's general decay.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 5 (Benji of Emperor An), the Treatise on the Western Qiang, the biography of Yu Xu, and the Annals of the Empresses; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 北乡侯 · 主要事迹

北乡侯刘懿是济北惠王之子。延光四年三月，[[e-han-an|安帝]]南巡崩于叶，阎皇后与兄阎显及宦官江京等定策，秘不发丧，还宫后立刘懿为帝——这是东汉又一次由后宫与外戚合谋的拥立。

刘懿在位约二百日即薨，史籍甚至未给他一个像样的本纪：他的存在，主要见于安帝纪之末与顺帝纪之首的夹缝。其治皆出阎氏，阎显兄弟与江京等权倾朝野，而帝本人无任何事迹可言。

十月，北乡侯薨。阎氏秘不发丧，欲更立他王，中黄门孙程等十九名宦官先发制人，斩江京，迎废太子济阴王[[e-han-shun|刘保]]即位，是为顺帝；阎后迁离宫，阎氏遂败。北乡侯不过二百日的「帝位」，成了阎氏与宦官两大势力对决的舞台布景，也是东汉最后一次「名分存疑」的准帝即位。

> 本地参考：点校本《后汉书》卷006《孝顺帝纪》、《安帝纪》、《皇后纪》、《宦者传》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Yi, Marquis of Beixiang, was a son of the king of Jibei. In the third month of the fourth Yanguang year,

died at Ye on his southern tour; Empress Yan, her brother Yan Xian, and the eunuch Jiang Jing settled the succession in secret, concealed the death, and raised Liu Yi to the throne upon their return to the palace — yet another enthronement engineered by the harem and the consorts.

He reigned about two hundred days before dying, and the histories did not even give him a proper benji: his existence is recorded mainly in the gap between the end of An's annals and the beginning of Shun's. All government issued from the Yan house; Yan Xian and his brothers with Jiang Jing dominated the court, while the emperor himself has no deeds whatever to his name.

In the tenth month the Marquis of Beixiang died. The Yans concealed the death, intending to raise another king; but the palace eunuch Sun Cheng and eighteen others struck first, slew Jiang Jing, and enthroned the deposed heir, the prince of Jiyin

, as Emperor Shun; Empress Yan was moved out of the palace and the Yan clan fell. The marquis's two hundred days of "reign" were the stage scenery for the showdown between the Yan faction and the eunuchs — and the last quasi-emperor enthronement of doubtful standing in Eastern Han.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 6 (Benji of Emperor Shun), ch. 5 (Emperor An), the Annals of the Empresses, and the biography of the Eunuchs; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉顺帝 · 主要事迹

刘保是[[e-han-an|安帝]]之子，永宁元年立为皇太子，延光三年以谗被废为济阴王。延光四年，北乡侯薨，宦官孙程等十九人斩江京、迎立济阴王，十一岁的刘保即位，是为顺帝——中国帝制史上第一次完全由宦官发动并完成的拥立。

顺帝一朝的政治结构由此定型：即位次年，十九侯同日封侯，宦官开始成为独立的政治力量；而外戚并未退场——阳嘉元年立梁妠为皇后，梁商、梁冀父子相继为大将军，梁氏之势在顺帝朝后半期全面养成。永和六年梁商薨，梁冀代为大将军，东汉最跋扈的一个外戚正式登场。

边事方面，永建二年班勇击匈奴呼衍王，西域诸国复通，是顺帝朝少数可称的武功；汉安元年遣杜乔、周举等八使巡行州郡，考察吏治，亦见整顿之志，然皆无补于大局。建康元年，顺帝崩，年三十。他死于梁氏权势的顶点，留下一个二岁的[[e-han-chong|冲帝]]与一份「权归后族」的遗产——史论所谓「顺帝之世，权归后族」，正是东汉中期政局最简洁的概括。

> 本地参考：点校本《后汉书》卷006《孝顺帝纪》、《宦者传》、《班勇传》、《梁冀传》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Bao was the son of

. Made heir apparent in the first Yongning year, he was deposed by slander as prince of Jiyin in the third Yanguang year. In the fourth Yanguang year the Marquis of Beixiang died, and the eunuch Sun Cheng with eighteen others slew Jiang Jing and enthroned the eleven-year-old prince of Jiyin as Emperor Shun — the first succession in Chinese imperial history accomplished entirely by eunuchs.

The structure of his reign was set from that moment: in the first year the nineteen eunuchs were enfeoffed on the same day, and the eunuchs became an independent political force. The consorts did not leave the stage: in the first Yangjia year Liang Na was made empress, and Liang Shang and then Liang Ji held the office of commander-in-chief; in the sixth Yonghe year Liang Shang died and Liang Ji succeeded — the most overbearing consort of Eastern Han now formally in power.

On the frontier, in the second Yongjian year Ban Yong struck the Xiongnu's Huyan king and the states of the Western Regions were reopened — one of the few deeds of Shun's reign worth the name; in the first Han'an year he sent Du Qiao, Zhou Ju, and six others to tour the provinces and inspect the officials, showing a will to reform that came to nothing against the larger drift. In the first Jiankang year Emperor Shun died at thirty. He died at the summit of Liang power, leaving a two-year-old

and the legacy summed up by the historians: "in the reign of Shun, power returned to the consort clan."

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 6 (Benji of Emperor Shun), and the biographies of the Eunuchs, Ban Yong, and Liang Ji; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉冲帝 · 主要事迹

刘炳是[[e-han-shun|顺帝]]之子，建康元年顺帝崩，年二岁的刘炳即位，梁太后临朝，梁冀秉政——东汉的幼主政治至此进入极端形态：皇帝小到连「系年」都嫌勉强。

冲帝在位约五个月。永嘉元年，九江等地盗贼蜂起，朝廷所面临的已是一个民变四起的帝国，而主政的梁氏一门正忙于巩固自己的权势。正月，冲帝崩于玉堂前殿，在位不足周岁，葬怀陵。梁太后与梁冀旋定策迎立渤海孝王之子刘缵，是为[[e-han-zhi|质帝]]。

冲帝之世没有留下任何属于他自己的政策或意志，甚至没有来得及形成自己的年号体系（永嘉为顺帝建康之后的改元，其治皆梁氏所为）。他存在的意义，在于证明东汉皇权已经空洞到可以由一个婴儿来填充——而下一个被填充进来的[[e-han-zhi|八岁质帝]]，将用一句「跋扈将军」结束自己，也揭开桓灵之世的大幕。

> 本地参考：点校本《后汉书》卷006《孝冲帝纪》、《梁冀传》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Bing was the son of

. When Shun died in the first Jiankang year, the two-year-old Bing took the throne, with Empress Dowager Liang in the regency and Liang Ji in power — Eastern Han's child-emperor politics now reaching its extreme form, a sovereign too small even for the courtesy of dating.

He reigned about five months. In the first Yongjia year bandits rose in force at Jiujiang and elsewhere: the court faced an empire of spreading revolt, while the Liang house was busy consolidating its own position. In the first month of the year he died in the front hall of the Yutang Palace, having reigned under a year, and was buried at Huailing. Empress Dowager Liang and Liang Ji then chose Liu Zuan, son of the filial king of Bohai, as

.

No policy, no will, not even a settled era-name system of his own belongs to Chong's reign (Yongjia was the era adopted after Jiankang, its government all Liang's doing). His significance is that the Han throne had grown empty enough to be filled by an infant — and the next infant to be filled in, the eight-year-old

, would end himself with the phrase "arrogant general," opening the curtain on the Huan-Ling age.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 6 (Benji of Emperor Chong) and the biography of Liang Ji; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 汉质帝 · 主要事迹

刘缵是渤海孝王刘鸿之子。永嘉元年[[e-han-chong|冲帝]]崩，梁太后与梁冀定策，迎年八岁的刘缵即位，是为质帝。这是他悲剧的开端，也是东汉梁氏专权最盛的时刻。

质帝幼而聪慧，史称「少聪敏」。本初元年，他在朝堂上直视梁冀，说了一句改变命运的话——「此跋扈将军也」。梁冀深恶之，同年闰六月，进毒饼弑帝。质帝中毒后尚能饮水求活，梁冀不许，帝遂崩，在位不过一年余。史家多惜其聪慧而哀其早夭：一个八岁的孩子，因为一句真话，成了东汉皇权与权臣对决的第一个牺牲品。

质帝死后，梁冀迎立蠡吾侯[[e-han-huan|刘志]]，是为桓帝。梁氏之祸又延续了十三年，直到延熹二年桓帝与宦官合谋诛梁氏。质帝之死是梁冀权势的注脚，也是东汉士人对「跋扈」一词最早的集体记忆——「跋扈将军」由此成为权臣的千古恶谥。

> 本地参考：点校本《后汉书》卷006《孝质帝纪》、《梁冀传》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Zuan was the son of the filial king Hong of Bohai. In the first Yongjia year, after

died, Empress Dowager Liang and Liang Ji chose the eight-year-old Zuan as Emperor Zhi. That was the beginning of his tragedy, and the summit of Liang autocracy in Eastern Han.

Zhi was sharp-witted as a child; the histories say he was "quick and clever from youth." In the first Benchu year, looking straight at Liang Ji in the court, he said the words that changed his life — "This is the arrogant general." Liang Ji hated him for it, and in the intercalary sixth month of the same year had poisoned cakes brought to the emperor. The poisoned boy begged for water to save himself; Liang Ji refused, and the emperor died, having reigned a little over a year. Historians have pitied the sharp boy and mourned his early end: an eight-year-old, killed for one true sentence, the first victim of the duel between Han sovereignty and its overbearing minister.

After Zhi's death Liang Ji raised the marquis of Liwu,

, as Emperor Huan, and the Liang scourge ran another thirteen years until Huan destroyed it with the eunuchs in the second Yanxi year. Zhi's death is the footnote to Liang Ji's power, and the origin of the士人's collective memory of the word "arrogant" — "the arrogant general" has been the eternal epithet of the overbearing minister ever since.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 6 (Benji of Emperor Zhi) and the biography of Liang Ji; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉桓帝 · 主要事迹

刘志是蠡吾侯刘翼之子。[[e-han-zhi|质帝]]被鸩后，梁冀迎立年十五的刘志，是为桓帝。此后的十四年，朝政尽在梁冀之手：梁冀一门前后七侯、三皇后、六贵人，专权二十年，百官侧目。

桓帝隐忍十四年，终于延熹二年抓住机会：借宦官单超、徐璜、具瑗、左悺、唐衡五人之力，发兵收梁冀大将军印，梁冀与其妻孙寿皆自杀，梁氏中外宗亲悉诛。然而以宦官诛外戚，代价是宦官集团取代外戚成为新的主宰——单超等五人同日封侯，史称「五侯」，宦官之祸自此转炽。延熹四年财用不足，减公卿以下俸，国力之窘可见一斑。

桓帝朝最深远的事件是党锢之祸：延熹九年，司隶校尉李膺等名士与宦官集团冲突激化，李膺等下狱，第一次党锢起；永康元年虽赦党人归田里，然禁锢终身。士人与宦官的对决，从此成为东汉末年政治的轴心。永康元年十二月，桓帝崩，年三十六，无嗣；窦武迎立解渎亭侯[[e-han-ling|刘宏]]，是为灵帝。史臣谓桓帝「前史残缺，尘垢负涂」，诛梁冀而纵五侯，实开灵帝之世宦官擅权的先声。

> 本地参考：点校本《后汉书》卷007《孝桓帝纪》、《梁冀传》、《宦者传》、《党锢列传》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Zhi was the son of the marquis Yi of Liwu. After

was poisoned, Liang Ji raised the fifteen-year-old Zhi to the throne as Emperor Huan. For the next fourteen years the government lay entirely in Liang Ji's hands: his house held seven marquises, three empresses, and six titled ladies, and ruled for twenty years while the ministers looked on askance.

Huan bided his time for fourteen years, and in the second Yanxi year seized his chance: using the eunuchs Shan Chao, Xu Huang, Ju Yuan, Zuo Guan, and Tang Heng, he sent troops to take Liang Ji's seal of office; Liang Ji and his wife Sun Shou killed themselves, and the entire Liang house, kin included, was destroyed. But the cure was worse than the disease: the eunuchs replaced the consorts as the dominant power — Shan Chao and the other four were enfeoffed the same day, the "Five Marquises," and the eunuch scourge burned brighter than ever. In the fourth Yanxi year salaries from the Three Excellencies down were cut for lack of funds — a measure of the realm's straits.

The deepest-reaching event of his reign was the proscription of the partisans: in the ninth Yanxi year the celebrity officials headed by Li Ying, colonel of the capital, clashed head-on with the eunuch faction; Li Ying and others were imprisoned and the first proscription began; in the first Yongkang year the partisans were pardoned and sent home, but barred from office for life. The duel between the scholar-officials and the eunuchs became the axis of late Eastern Han politics from this point on. In the twelfth month of Yongkang 1, Huan died at thirty-six, without issue; Dou Wu raised the marquis of Xieduting,

, as Emperor Ling. The historians wrote that Huan's earlier records are fragmentary and "dirtied with dust" — he destroyed Liang Ji only to unleash the Five Marquises, sounding the prelude to the eunuch autocracy of Ling's reign.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 7 (Benji of Emperor Huan), and the biographies of Liang Ji, the Eunuchs, and the Proscribed Partisans; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉灵帝 · 主要事迹

刘宏是解渎亭侯刘苌之子。[[e-han-huan|桓帝]]崩而无嗣，窦太后与窦武迎立年十二的刘宏，是为灵帝——东汉末年的序幕，由此拉开。

即位当年，窦武、陈蕃谋诛宦官而事败身死，宦官集团反扑，第二次党锢起，天下名士禁锢者六七百人。此后灵帝的二十余年，宦官与外戚交替掌权，而皇帝本人则把精力投向了另一件事：光和元年开西园卖官，公卿州郡各有定价，「三公」亦可买；同年置鸿都门学，以书画尺牍取士，与太学儒生分庭抗礼。中平二年造万金堂，聚钱西园——汉家四百年基业，在灵帝手中成了可以标价出售的东西。

中平元年，巨鹿张角以太平道聚众，黄巾起义爆发，「八州并起，天下响应」。灵帝赦党人以求合力镇压，命皇甫嵩、朱儁等讨平之，然而州郡牧守之权自此渐重，豪强各自拥兵，汉室之土已呈瓦解之势。中平五年置西园八校尉，袁绍、曹操等皆在其列——这支皇帝亲军，日后将变成群雄争霸的班底。

中平六年，灵帝崩，年三十四。他留下的帝国已千疮百孔：宦官与士人势同水火，黄巾余部遍布州郡，边地军阀虎视眈眈。[[e-han-shao-bian|少帝辩]]即位数月即被董卓所废，东汉遂入末世。

> 本地参考：点校本《后汉书》卷008《孝灵帝纪》、《党锢列传》、《陈蕃传》、《皇甫嵩传》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Hong was the son of the marquis Chang of Xieduting.

died without issue, and Empress Dowager Dou with Dou Wu raised the twelve-year-old Hong as Emperor Ling — the curtain rises on the last act of Eastern Han.

In the very first year of his reign, Dou Wu and Chen Fan's plot against the eunuchs failed and cost them their lives; the eunuchs struck back, the second proscription began, and six or seven hundred famous men of the realm were barred from office. For the next twenty years the eunuchs and the consorts took turns at power while the emperor turned his attention elsewhere: in the first Guanghe year he opened office sales at the West Garden, with set prices for dukes, ministers, and provincial governors — even the Three Dukes could be bought; in the same year he founded the Hongdu Academy, choosing scholars for calligraphy and letters against the classicists of the Grand Academy; in the second Zhongping year he built the Hall of Ten Thousand Gold to hoard money at the West Garden. Four hundred years of the Han inheritance had become, in Ling's hands, goods with a price tag.

In the first Zhongping year Zhang Jiao of Julu gathered followers through the Way of Great Peace, and the Yellow Turban revolt erupted — "eight provinces rose together, and the realm answered." Ling lifted the proscription to rally the scholars, and Huangfu Song and Zhu Jun suppressed the revolt; but the power of provincial governors grew from that war, and the regional strongmen each held troops of their own. The realm of Han was already coming apart. In the fifth Zhongping year he created the Eight Colonels of the West Garden, among them Yuan Shao and Cao Cao — this imperial guard would become the roster of the coming warlord age.

In the sixth Zhongping year Ling died at thirty-four, leaving an empire in tatters: eunuchs and scholars at each other's throats, Yellow Turban remnants across the provinces, and frontier warlords closing in.

was deposed by Dong Zhuo within months, and Eastern Han entered its last age.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉少帝辩 · 主要事迹

刘辩是[[e-han-ling|灵帝]]之子，何皇后所生。中平六年灵帝崩，辩即位，何太后临朝，大将军何进秉政。东汉的最后一场宫廷剧，就在这几个月内演完。

何进欲诛宦官，却迟疑不决，反召四方兵将入京示威——包括并州牧董卓。事泄，宦官张让等先发制人，杀何进；袁绍等率兵入宫，尽诛宦官二千余人，「十常侍乱」的结局，是宦官与外戚同归于尽。随后入京的董卓成了唯一的赢家：九月，董卓废少帝辩为弘农王，立陈留王刘协，即[[e-han-xian|献帝]]。

辩在位不足半年，被废后幽于阁上。初平元年正月，董卓遣郎中令李儒进鸩，辩临终与妻唐姬作诀别歌，时年十四。他一生没有做过任何决策，却亲身见证了东汉皇权最后的崩塌：在他之前，皇帝尚是外戚与宦官争夺的猎物；在他之后，皇帝成了军阀手里的印玺。

> 本地参考：点校本《后汉书》卷008《孝灵帝纪》、卷009《孝献帝纪》、《董卓传》、《何进传》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。
