bio_parts_en.value: Liu Bian was the son of

by Empress He. When Ling died in the sixth Zhongping year, Bian took the throne with Empress Dowager He in the regency and General-in-Chief He Jin in power. The last court drama of Eastern Han was played out in these few months.

He Jin meant to destroy the eunuchs, but hesitated and instead summoned troops from the provinces to overawe the court — including Dong Zhuo, governor of Bingzhou. The plot leaked; the eunuchs led by Zhang Rang struck first and slew He Jin; Yuan Shao and others stormed the palace and slaughtered more than two thousand eunuchs. The "chaos of the Ten Attendants" ended with eunuchs and consorts destroying each other. Dong Zhuo, arriving on cue, was the sole victor: in the ninth month he deposed Bian as Prince of Hongnong and raised the prince of Chenliu, Xie, as

.

Bian had reigned under half a year. Deposed, he was shut up in a tower; in the first month of the first Chuping year Dong Zhuo sent Li Ru with poisoned wine. Bian sang a farewell to his wife Tang Ji as he drank, and died at fourteen. He never made a single decision of his own, yet he witnessed the final collapse of Han sovereignty: before him the emperor had been the prize fought over by consorts and eunuchs; after him, the emperor became a seal in the hands of warlords.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 8 (Benji of Emperor Ling), ch. 9 (Benji of Emperor Xian), and the biographies of Dong Zhuo and He Jin; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). emperors.bio_md:
# 汉献帝 · 主要事迹

刘协是[[e-han-ling|灵帝]]次子。中平六年，董卓废[[e-han-shao-bian|少帝辩]]，立年九岁的刘协，是为献帝——汉家四百年天下的最后一位皇帝，从此开始了他作为「流动的玉玺」的三十一年。

初平元年，董卓逼迁长安，焚洛阳宫室，东汉中枢第一次流离失所；初平三年，王允与吕布诛董卓，旋为李傕、郭汜所败，长安再乱。兴平二年，献帝出长安东归，一路为乱兵所劫，食枣栗度日，流离曹阳、弘农之间。建安元年，曹操迎帝都许，「奉天子以令不臣」——献帝终于有了一个固定的都城，也终于有了一个不可摆脱的主人。

都许之后的二十四年，是曹操父子经营天下的二十四年，也是献帝作为禅让道具的二十四年：建安五年官渡之战、十三年赤壁之战，皆在许都的名义下进行；建安十九年，曹操杀伏皇后，献帝只能默然；二十五年（延康元年），曹丕受禅，献帝逊位，封山阳公，东汉正式灭亡。他做了三十一年皇帝，从未有过一天的实权，却以「建安」年号为名，见证了整个三国格局的形成。

逊位后的献帝在山阳做了十四年公，于魏明帝青龙二年薨，年五十四，以汉天子礼葬。史评「得位屯蹇，版荡云海」，正是他一生最贴切的注脚：汉祚四百年，始于[[e-han-guangwu|光武]]之中兴，终于献帝之禅代。

> 本地参考：点校本《后汉书》卷009《孝献帝纪》、《董卓传》，《三国志》武帝纪、文帝纪，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Xie was the second son of
. In the sixth Zhongping year, Dong Zhuo deposed

and raised the nine-year-old Xie as Emperor Xian — the last emperor of the four-hundred-year Han, beginning his thirty-one years as a "movable imperial seal."

In the first Chuping year Dong Zhuo forced the court to Chang'an, burning the palaces of Luoyang: the Eastern Han center was uprooted for the first time. In the third Chuping year Wang Yun and Lü Bu killed Dong Zhuo, only to be overthrown by Li Jue and Guo Si; Chang'an fell into chaos again. In the second Xingping year the emperor left Chang'an and fled east, robbed by the soldiery on the road, living on dates and chestnuts, drifting through Caoyang and Hongnong. In the first Jian'an year Cao Cao received the emperor and settled the court at Xu — "supporting the Son of Heaven to command the disobedient." Xian at last had a fixed capital, and at last a master he could never shake.

The twenty-four years at Xu were the years of the Cao house's conquest of the realm, and of Xian's role as the prop of an abdication: the Guandu campaign of Jian'an 5 and the Red Cliffs of Jian'an 13 were fought under his name; in Jian'an 19 Cao Cao slew Empress Fu, and Xian could only be silent; in the first Yankang year (220) Cao Pi received the abdication, and Xian was enfeoffed Duke of Shanyang. Eastern Han was formally finished. He had been emperor for thirty-one years without a single day of real power, yet under his "Jian'an" era name the whole Three Kingdoms pattern took shape.

As Duke of Shanyang he lived another fourteen years, dying in the second Qinglong year of Wei at fifty-four, buried with the rites of a Han emperor. The historians' verdict — "he got the throne in hardship and drifting, tossed on the waves of the age" — fits him exactly: the Han mandate, opened by

's restoration, closed with Xian's abdication.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 9 (Benji of Emperor Xian) and the biography of Dong Zhuo; the *Sanguozhi*, biographies of Emperor Wu (Cao Cao) and Emperor Wen (Cao Pi); Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). emperors.summary_en: The founding emperor of Liang, who reigned for nearly half a century, promoted letters and Buddhist learning to a Southern Dynasties cultural peak, and late in life took in Hou Jing—dying trapped in the besieged palace city of Taicheng.

timeline.title: 起兵建康
timeline.summary: 自襄阳东下攻入建康，掌控南齐残局。
timeline.summary_en: He marched east from Xiangyang and stormed Jiankang, seizing control of Southern Qi's endgame.

timeline.title: 受禅建梁
timeline.summary: 齐禅于梁，萧衍即帝位，梁朝建立。
timeline.summary_en: Qi abdicated to Liang; Xiao Yan took the throne and the Liang dynasty was founded.

timeline.title: 置五经博士等
timeline.summary: 开国文教措置，梁武前半文治基础。
timeline.summary_en: Foundational cultural measures that grounded the civil governance of his first half-reign.

timeline.title: 作浮山堰
timeline.summary: 堰淮攻魏，工程巨大而争议。
timeline.summary_en: A vast, controversial project damming the Huai River to attack Wei.

timeline.title: 同泰寺开基叙事
timeline.summary: 同泰佛事升级，舍身前史。
timeline.summary_en: Buddhist rites at Tongtai Temple escalated—the prelude to his self-surrenders.

timeline.title: 舍身同泰
timeline.summary: 数次舍身同泰寺，群臣以钱奉赎，佛事与财政绑定，成史著名场面。
timeline.summary_en: He repeatedly surrendered himself to Tongtai Temple and was ransomed by his officials, binding Buddhist rites to state finances—a famous scene in history.

timeline.title: 侯景来降决策
timeline.summary: 纳降争论，战略误判前奏。
timeline.summary_en: The debate over accepting the defector—the prelude to a strategic misjudgment.

timeline.title: 台城被围
timeline.summary: 侯景围台城，梁政崩溃。
timeline.summary_en: Hou Jing besieged Taicheng; Liang governance collapsed.

timeline.title: 纳侯景
timeline.summary: 接受侯景，旋即爆发侯景之乱，建康遭灾。
timeline.summary_en: Hou Jing was accepted; his rebellion erupted soon after, devastating Jiankang.

timeline.title: 台城饿死
timeline.summary: 台城陷后，武帝被制，忧愤饥病而崩。
timeline.summary_en: After Taicheng fell, Emperor Wu was held under control and died of grief, hunger, and illness.

timeline.title: 简文继位对照
timeline.summary: 武帝崩后简文立，侯景仍控建康。
timeline.summary_en: After Emperor Wu's death, Jianwen succeeded while Hou Jing still controlled Jiankang.

timeline.title: 文化全盛
timeline.summary: 长年安定，文学、佛学、礼乐兴盛，南朝文化高峰之一。
timeline.summary_en: Decades of stability brought flourishing letters, Buddhist learning, and ritual music—one of the Southern Dynasties' cultural peaks.

emperors.bio_md:
# 梁武帝 · 主要事迹

萧衍是梁朝的开国之君。中兴元年（501），他自襄阳东下攻入建康，掌控南齐残局；次年受齐禅即帝位，梁朝由此建立，仍都建康。此后在位近半个世纪，是本图鉴中治世最长的皇帝之一。

开国之初，他置五经博士、振兴文教；天监至大同间长年安定，文学、佛学、礼乐并盛，被推为南朝文化的高峰之一。对外则有天监十三年（514）的浮山堰工程，堰淮水以攻魏，规模巨大而备受争议。

他的另一面是佞佛。大通元年（527）起，同泰寺佛事不断升级，他屡次舍身入寺，由群臣以钱奉赎，佛事与国家财政就此绑定。

晚年的转折在太清元年（547）：侯景来降，纳降之议争论激烈，他最终决定接受。次年侯景之乱爆发，建康遭灾，台城被围；太清三年（549）台城陷落，武帝为侯景所制，忧愤饥病而崩。简文帝随后继位，侯景仍控建康。前半英主、后半困于佛与侯景，正是本朝月旦的两面。

与[[n-wei-xiaowen|北魏孝文帝]]对读：一北一南，一个以汉化改革重铸北魏，一个以文教与佛事撑起南朝文化高峰；而台城之困，则为南朝由盛转衰写下注脚。

bio_parts_en.value:
Xiao Yan was the founding ruler of the Liang dynasty. In Zhongxing 1 (501) he marched east from Xiangyang, stormed Jiankang, and seized control of Southern Qi's endgame; the next year he accepted Qi's abdication and took the throne, founding Liang with the capital still at Jiankang. He would reign for nearly half a century—one of the longest reigns in this atlas.

At the founding he appointed Erudites of the Five Classics and revived letters and learning; the long stability from Tianjian to Datong brought literature, Buddhist learning, and ritual music to a simultaneous flowering, counted among the cultural peaks of the Southern Dynasties. In foreign ventures there was the Fushan Weir project of Tianjian 13 (514), damming the Huai River to attack Wei—a vast and deeply controversial work.

His other face was his devotion to Buddhism. From Datong 1 (527) the rites at Tongtai Temple escalated steadily; he repeatedly surrendered himself to the temple and was ransomed by his officials at great price, binding Buddhist ceremony to the state treasury.

The late-reign turning point came in Taiqing 1 (547): Hou Jing came offering his allegiance, and though the debate over accepting him was fierce, Xiao Yan finally decided to take him in. The next year the Hou Jing Rebellion erupted, disaster struck Jiankang, and Taicheng was besieged; in Taiqing 3 (549) Taicheng fell, and Emperor Wu, held under Hou Jing's control, died of grief, hunger, and illness. Emperor Jianwen succeeded him while Hou Jing still held Jiankang. The able ruler of the first half, the man trapped by Buddha and Hou Jing in the second—these are the two faces of the verdict on his reign.

Read alongside

: one north, one south; one recast Northern Wei through sinicizing reform, the other sustained a Southern Dynasties cultural peak through letters and Buddhist devotion. And the siege of Taicheng wrote the footnote to the Southern Dynasties' turn from height to decline.

emperors.summary_en: The Northern Wei emperor whose iron cavalry destroyed Hu Xia, Northern Yan, and Northern Liang to unify the north; he campaigned south to the Yangzi and suppressed Buddhism in his late years, and at the height of his military power was murdered by a close attendant.

timeline.title: 即位
timeline.summary: 明元帝崩，焘即位，北魏进入扩张高峰。
timeline.summary_en: Emperor Mingyuan died and Tuoba Tao succeeded; Northern Wei entered its peak of expansion.

timeline.title: 改元与亲征开局
timeline.summary: 即位后改元更始，朝廷人事随新主调整，北魏扩张加速。
timeline.summary_en: After his accession he changed the era name and court personnel followed the new ruler; Northern Wei's expansion accelerated.

timeline.title: 取统万
timeline.summary: 攻取胡夏都城统万，灭夏关键一战。
timeline.summary_en: He captured Tongwan, capital of Hu Xia—the decisive blow against Xia.

timeline.title: 灭胡夏
timeline.summary: 灭赫连夏，取关中。
timeline.summary_en: He destroyed the Helian Xia and took the Guanzhong region.

timeline.title: 灭北燕
timeline.summary: 灭冯氏北燕，辽西归魏。
timeline.summary_en: He destroyed the Feng family's Northern Yan; western Liaoning fell to Wei.

timeline.title: 凉州平
timeline.summary: 兵至姑臧，凉州平定。
timeline.summary_en: Wei troops reached Guzang and Liangzhou was pacified.

timeline.title: 灭北凉
timeline.summary: 灭沮渠北凉，北方统一于北魏，十六国阶段落幕。
timeline.summary_en: He destroyed the Juqu Northern Liang; the north was unified under Northern Wei and the Sixteen Kingdoms period ended.

timeline.title: 真君灭佛
timeline.summary: 太平真君年间禁佛毁寺，宗教政策极端化。
timeline.summary_en: During the Taiping Zhenjun era Buddhism was banned and temples destroyed—religious policy turned extreme.

timeline.title: 盖吴起兵
timeline.summary: 关中盖吴反，魏军镇压。
timeline.summary_en: Ge Wu rose in Guanzhong and was suppressed by Wei forces.

timeline.title: 诏诸州坑沙门
timeline.summary: 灭佛政策达于高峰。
timeline.summary_en: The persecution of Buddhism reached its peak.

timeline.title: 南征瓜步
timeline.summary: 大举南征刘宋，至瓜步，与宋文帝隔江对峙，威震而未能定南。
timeline.summary_en: A massive campaign against Liu Song reached Guabu, facing Emperor Wen of Song across the Yangzi—awe-inspiring, yet unable to conquer the south.

timeline.title: 被弑
timeline.summary: 为中常侍宗爱所弑，北魏政局动荡。
timeline.summary_en: He was murdered by the palace attendant Zong Ai, and Northern Wei politics fell into turmoil.

emperors.bio_md:
# 太武帝 · 主要事迹

拓跋焘是北魏第三位皇帝。泰常八年（423）明元帝崩，他即位于平城，明年改元始光；在位二十九年，北魏自此进入扩张高峰。本页以《魏书·世祖纪》为年表主线，灭佛诸事互见《魏书·释老志》。

他的武功是本纪最硬的一条线：始光四年（427）攻取胡夏都城统万，神䴥四年（431）灭赫连夏、取关中，太延二年（436）灭冯氏北燕、辽西归魏，太延五年（439）兵至姑臧、灭沮渠北凉。至此北方统一于北魏，十六国阶段落幕。

武功之外，内政与宗教政策同样醒目。太平真君六年（445）关中盖吴起兵，魏军镇压；而自太平真君五年（444）起，朝廷禁佛毁寺，至七年（446）诏诸州坑沙门，灭佛政策达于高峰。档案将崔浩、寇谦之列为其宗教转向的关联人物，这也是后世评价中争议最集中的一面。

太平真君十一年（450），他大举南征刘宋，兵锋直抵长江北岸的瓜步，与宋文帝隔江对峙，威震江淮而终未能定南。正平二年（452），他在平城为中常侍宗爱所弑，北魏政局随之动荡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Tuoba Tao was the third emperor of Northern Wei. In Taichang 8 (423) Emperor Mingyuan died and he ascended the throne at Pingcheng, changing the era name to Shiguang the following year; over twenty-nine years on the throne, Northern Wei entered its peak of expansion. This page takes 《魏书·世祖纪》 as the backbone of its chronology; the persecution of Buddhism is cross-referenced in 《魏书·释老志》.

His martial record is the hardest line in his annals: in Shiguang 4 (427) he captured Tongwan, capital of Hu Xia; in Shenjia 4 (431) he destroyed the Helian Xia and took Guanzhong; in Taiyan 2 (436) he destroyed the Feng family's Northern Yan and western Liaoning fell to Wei; in Taiyan 5 (439) his troops reached Guzang and destroyed the Juqu Northern Liang. With that, the north was unified under Northern Wei, and the Sixteen Kingdoms period came to an end.

Beyond the campaigns, domestic and religious policy were no less striking. In Taiping Zhenjun 6 (445) Ge Wu rose in revolt in Guanzhong and was put down by Wei forces; from Taiping Zhenjun 5 (444) the court banned Buddhism and destroyed temples, and in Zhenjun 7 (446) an edict ordered the provinces to bury monks alive—the persecution reached its peak. The record names Cui Hao and Kou Qianzhi as figures tied to his religious turn, and this remains the most contested side of his later reputation.

In Taiping Zhenjun 11 (450) he launched a massive southern campaign against Liu Song, driving straight to Guabu on the north bank of the Yangzi and facing Emperor Wen of Song across the river—an awesome display that still failed to settle the south. In Zhengping 2 (452) he was murdered at Pingcheng by the palace attendant Zong Ai, and Northern Wei politics fell into turmoil.

A thread for reading across pages: set against his successor

, one sees Northern Wei's long turn from cavalry expansion to sinicizing reform; the juxtaposition of supreme military achievement with the persecution of Buddhism and a murdered emperor's end is exactly why the appraisal of him runs neutral-to-negative.

timeline.summary: 文明太后执政高峰，改革铺垫。

timeline.title: 班禄制

timeline.summary_en: Salaries were granted to reward integrity and discipline the bureaucracy—a key step in the Taihe New Policies.

timeline.title: 均田制

timeline.summary_en: The equal-field system was promulgated, deeply shaping later Sui–Tang debates on land tenure.

timeline.title: 三长制
timeline.summary: 立三长，基层组织改革。
timeline.summary_en: The three-elders system was set up, reforming grassroots administration.

timeline.title: 迁都洛阳

timeline.title: 禁胡服胡语

timeline.title: 定族姓

timeline.summary_en: Aristocratic clan rankings were fixed, hastening the elite's gentrification.

timeline.title: 太子恂废

timeline.summary_en: The crown prince, who had resisted sinicization, was deposed—the price of reform.

timeline.title: 改姓元

timeline.title: 南伐襄阳线

emperors.bio_md:
# 孝文帝 · 主要事迹

元宏（本姓拓跋）是读南北朝史绕不开的改制枢纽。延兴元年（471）幼年即位于平城，前期由文明冯太后临朝主政；本页以《魏书·高祖纪》（卷007上下）为年表主线，辅以《魏书》皇后传、食货志互见与《资治通鉴》对应年段编年对照。

太和年间，班禄制（太和八年）以禄酬廉、整顿吏治，均田制（太和九年）颁行并深远影响隋唐田制讨论，三长制（太和十年）重建基层组织——这套太和新政构成改革的制度骨架。

太和十七年（493）以南伐为名迁都洛阳，北魏政治中心南移；随后禁胡服胡语、定门阀族姓、改拓跋为元姓，汉化全面铺开。改革代价同样清晰：太和二十年（496），反抗汉化的太子元恂被废，宫廷震荡。

晚年持续南伐襄阳一线，消耗国力；太和二十三年（499）崩于南征军中，归葬洛阳。汉化路线由宣武延续，而激进改制与六镇矛盾的争议亦由此埋下。与[[n-wei-taiwu|太武帝]]对读：一先以武功完成北方统一，一以改制重塑王朝面貌——北魏的两副面孔在此分合。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yuan Hong (born into the Tuoba clan) is a pivot of institutional reform that no reader of the Northern and Southern Dynasties can bypass. He ascended the throne as a child at Pingcheng in Yanxing 1 (471), with Empress Dowager Wenming (Feng) ruling as regent in his early years. This page takes 《魏书·高祖纪》（卷007上下） as the backbone of its chronology, cross-checked against the empresses' biographies (皇后传) and the Treatise on Food and Money (食货志) in the Book of Wei, and against the corresponding annals of 《资治通鉴》.

During the Taihe era, the salary system (Taihe 8) paid officials to reward integrity and discipline the bureaucracy; the equal-field system (Taihe 9) was promulgated and would deeply shape Sui–Tang debates on land tenure; and the three-elders system (Taihe 10) rebuilt grassroots administration. Together these Taihe New Policies formed the institutional skeleton of the reform.

In Taihe 17 (493), under the pretext of a southern campaign, he moved the capital to Luoyang, shifting Northern Wei's political center south. There followed the ban on Hu dress and speech, the fixing of aristocratic clan rankings, and the change of the Tuoba surname to Yuan—sinicization rolled out in full. The costs were equally clear: in Taihe 20 (496), Crown Prince Yuan Xun, who had resisted sinicization, was deposed, shaking the palace.

In his final years he campaigned persistently on the Xiangyang front, draining the state's strength; in Taihe 23 (499) he died in the army during a southern campaign and was buried back at Luoyang. The sinicization line was carried on by Xuanwu, while the controversies of radical reform and the tensions with the Six Garrisons were sown here as well. Read alongside
: one first completed the unification of the north by arms, the other remade the dynasty's face through institutional reform—the two faces of Northern Wei meet and part in these two men.

emperors.summary: 从被掠卖为奴的羯人少年到开国称帝，都襄国、灭前赵而臣北方，十六国最具戏剧性的创业者。
emperors.summary_en: A Jie youth kidnapped and sold into slavery who rose to found an empire — ruling from Xiangguo, he destroyed Former Zhao and made the north submit, the most dramatic state-founder of the Sixteen Kingdoms.

portrait.appearance_basis: 羯人，史载重其雄略。MVP 用占位图；定稿前依时代冠服作艺术想象。

timeline.title: 被掠为奴
timeline.summary: 羯人石勒少时被掠卖为奴，后聚众起兵，是十六国最戏剧性的社会流动叙事。
timeline.summary_en: Shi Le, a Jie, was kidnapped and sold into slavery in his youth and later gathered a following to rise in arms — the Sixteen Kingdoms' most dramatic story of social mobility.

timeline.title: 依附汉赵
timeline.summary: 一度归刘渊、刘聪系统，在华北作战中积累实力。
timeline.summary_en: For a time he attached himself to the Han-Zhao system of Liu Yuan and Liu Cong, building strength in the north China campaigns.

timeline.title: 攻陷洛阳相关
timeline.summary: 参与永嘉之乱后华北混战，军势坐大。
timeline.summary_en: He joined the melee in north China that followed the Yongjia upheaval, and his military power swelled.

timeline.title: 襄国称赵
timeline.summary: 称赵王，都襄国，后赵政权成立，脱离前赵阴影。
timeline.summary_en: He took the title King of Zhao and made Xiangguo his capital; the Later Zhao regime was founded, out of Former Zhao's shadow.

timeline.title: 称大单于赵王进阶
timeline.title_en: Great Chanyu and King of Zhao
timeline.summary: 名号与制度升格，后赵雏形稳固。
timeline.summary_en: His titles and institutions were elevated, and the Later Zhao framework stabilized.

timeline.title: 洛阳大战前
timeline.summary: 与刘曜对峙升级，灭赵前夜。
timeline.summary_en: The standoff with Liu Yao escalated — the eve of Zhao's destruction.

timeline.title: 灭前赵
timeline.summary: 破刘曜，灭前赵，北方大部归后赵。
timeline.summary_en: He defeated Liu Yao and destroyed Former Zhao; most of the north fell to Later Zhao.

timeline.title: 称帝
timeline.summary: 称皇帝，后赵帝制完备。
timeline.summary_en: He took the title of emperor, completing Later Zhao's imperial system.

timeline.title: 胡汉分治与学校
timeline.summary: 设君子营、兴学校等，胡汉秩序探索。
timeline.summary_en: He established the Gentlemen's Camp, promoted schools, and explored a Hu-Han order.

timeline.title: 重用张宾
timeline.summary: 以张宾为谋主，兴学校、定制度，胡汉分治中有秩序建设。

emperors.bio_md:
# 后赵高祖 · 主要事迹

石勒是羯人，少时约当西晋永兴前后被掠卖为奴，后来聚众起兵，最终登上帝位——从奴隶到天子的跨度，使他成为十六国史里最戏剧性的创业者。本页以《晋书》卷一百四至一百五石勒载记为年表主线，辅以《资治通鉴》编年（本地参考库已备）。

创业之初，他一度归入刘渊、刘聪的汉赵系统，借汉赵旗帜在华北作战中积累实力。永嘉五年（311）洛阳陷落前后，他参与永嘉之乱后的华北混战，军势迅速坐大，成为割据一方的主力。

太兴二年（319），石勒称赵王、都襄国，正式脱离前赵阴影，后赵政权由此成立；两年后进称大单于，名号与制度同步升格。咸和三年至四年（328–329），他与前赵末主刘曜在洛阳一线决战，破刘曜、灭前赵，北方大部归入后赵版图。咸和五年（330），他在襄国称皇帝，帝制完备，完成了从奴隶到天子的全过程。

石勒并非只有武功。他以张宾为谋主，兴学校、定制度，设君子营安置士人，在胡汉分治的框架下做秩序建设的探索。需要注意，史籍中后赵的残暴记载多须区分石勒本人与其后继者石虎；对石勒本人，史家仍称其雄略。

咸和八年（333），石勒崩于襄国。他生前安排的继承人石弘旋即为石虎所夺，后赵政治迅速恶化，国祚不长。与[[q-qin-fu-jian|前秦苻坚]]对读：同为十六国胡人政权的立国或中兴之主，一前一后，可见那个时代创业与治乱的不同路径。

bio_parts_en.value:
Shi Le was a Jie. In his youth, around the Yongxing era of the Western Jin, he was kidnapped and sold into slavery; he later gathered a following, rose in arms, and finally ascended the imperial throne — the span from slave to Son of Heaven makes him the most dramatic state-founder in the history of the Sixteen Kingdoms. This page takes the Shi Le annals in juan 104–105 of the 《晋书》 as its chronological backbone, supplemented by the chronicle of the 《资治通鉴》 (available in the local reference library).

At the start of his enterprise he attached himself for a time to the Han-Zhao system of Liu Yuan and Liu Cong, building strength through campaigns in north China under the Han-Zhao banner. Around the fall of Luoyang in Yongjia 5 (311), he joined the melee that followed the Yongjia upheaval in north China; his military power swelled rapidly, making him a leading force among the regional powers.

In Taixing 2 (319) Shi Le took the title King of Zhao and made Xiangguo his capital, formally stepping out of Former Zhao's shadow — the Later Zhao regime was thereby founded; two years later he advanced to Great Chanyu, his titles and institutions rising in step. In Xianhe 3–4 (328–329) he fought the decisive battle along the Luoyang line against Liu Yao, the last ruler of Former Zhao: he defeated Liu Yao, destroyed Former Zhao, and most of the north entered the Later Zhao map. In Xianhe 5 (330) he proclaimed himself emperor at Xiangguo, completing the imperial system — and with it the entire passage from slave to Son of Heaven.

Shi Le was not a man of martial feats alone. He made Zhang Bin his chief strategist, promoted schools and fixed institutions, established the Gentlemen's Camp to house men of letters, and explored the building of order within the framework of Hu-Han dual rule. One caveat: the records of Later Zhao cruelty in the histories must often be divided between Shi Le himself and his successor Shi Hu; of Shi Le himself, historians still speak of his boldness of design.

In Xianhe 8 (333) Shi Le died at Xiangguo. Shi Hong, the heir he had arranged, was at once dispossessed by Shi Hu; Later Zhao politics deteriorated quickly, and the dynastic line did not last long. Read him against
: both were founders or restorers of Hu states in the Sixteen Kingdoms period, one earlier and one later, and together they show the era's different paths of state-building and of order and collapse.

emperors.bio_md:
# 前秦世祖 · 主要事迹

苻坚（357—385 在位）是十六国时期最接近统一天下的前秦君主。永兴元年（357）他诛暴主苻生，即天王位，改元永兴，前秦由此进入苻坚时代。本页以《晋书·苻坚载记》（卷113–114）为年表主线，辅以《资治通鉴·晋纪》编年对照。

即位之后，他把国政委于王猛。王猛整肃吏治、打击贵戚，前秦国力急升，构成苻坚一朝的文治底色。武功随之而起：太和五年（370）王猛克邺，前燕遂灭，北方统一进程加速；太元元年（376）再灭前凉，兼及代地，河西归于前秦，北方大体统一，版图臻于巅峰。

巅峰之后是急转。太元七年（382）朝议伐晋，其时王猛已卒，谏阻无力；次年苻坚决意南伐，史载有「投鞭于江，足断其流」一类豪语，倾国出兵。太元八年（383）淝水一战大败于东晋谢安、谢玄一系，前秦由此崩解，各族复起。需要说明的是，「投鞭断流」语出记载的文学性颇浓，但南伐的战略责任归于苻坚本人，这一点仍成立。

太元九年（384）慕容垂独立，燕秦瓦解；次年苻坚西奔五将山一带，为姚苌所害，前秦迅速瓦解。读苻坚，可与[[n-wei-taiwu|太武帝]]对读：两者皆以武力整合北方，一败于南征而国解，一再合北方而开启北朝，可见十六国北朝兴亡的节奏。

bio_parts_en.value:
Fu Jian (r. 357–385) was the Former Qin ruler who came closest to unifying all under Heaven in the Sixteen Kingdoms period. In Yongxing 1 (357) he executed the tyrannical ruler Fu Sheng, took the title Heavenly King, and changed the era name to Yongxing; Former Qin thereby entered the age of Fu Jian. This page takes the 《晋书·苻坚载记》 (juan 113–114) as its chronological backbone, checked against the chronicle of the 《资治通鉴·晋纪》.

After his enthronement he entrusted the affairs of state to Wang Meng. Wang Meng disciplined the bureaucracy and struck at powerful kinsmen; Former Qin's strength surged, forming the civil-government foundation of Fu Jian's reign. Military achievement followed: in Taihe 5 (370) Wang Meng took Ye, Former Yan was destroyed, and the unification of the north accelerated; in Taiyuan 1 (376) he further destroyed Former Liang, reaching as far as the land of Dai; Hexi fell to Former Qin, the north was largely unified, and the map reached its peak.

After the peak came the sharp turn. In Taiyuan 7 (382) the court debated attacking Jin; Wang Meng was already dead, and remonstrance carried no force. The next year Fu Jian resolved on the southern campaign — the histories record boasts of the sort "throw our whips into the river and they would dam its flow" — and mobilized the entire state. In Taiyuan 8 (383), at the single battle of the Fei River, he was crushingly defeated by the Eastern Jin line of Xie An and Xie Xuan; Former Qin disintegrated and the various peoples rose again. It should be noted that the phrase "whips damming the river" carries a strong literary coloring in the sources, but strategic responsibility for the southern campaign rests with Fu Jian himself — that point still stands.

In Taiyuan 9 (384) Murong Chui declared independence and the Yan-Qin order collapsed; the next year Fu Jian fled west to the Wujiangshan area, where he was killed by Yao Chang, and Former Qin rapidly fell apart. Reading Fu Jian, one may set him against

: both integrated the north by force; one broke on a southern campaign and lost his state, the other re-unified the north and opened the Northern Dynasties — together they show the rhythm of rise and fall across the Sixteen Kingdoms and Northern Dynasties.

emperors.summary: 1038年称帝建大夏，创西夏文、立番汉官制，三败宋军而与宋辽鼎立的西夏开国之主。
emperors.summary_en: The founding ruler of Western Xia, who proclaimed himself emperor of Great Xia in 1038, created the Tangut script and a dual Tangut–Han official system, defeated Song armies three times, and stood as a third power alongside Song and Liao.

portrait.appearance_basis: 《宋史》卷485夏国传：「性雄毅，多大略，善绘画……圆面高准，身长五尺余。少时好衣长袖绯衣，冠黑冠，佩弓矢。」定稿前依此容貌与冠服描写作艺术想象。

timeline.title: 袭夏王位
timeline.summary: 李德明卒，元昊嗣位，加速去宋化与民族国家建构。
timeline.summary_en: On Li Deming's death, Yuanhao succeeded and accelerated de-Songification and nation-building.

timeline.title: 创制西夏文
timeline.summary: 命野利仁荣等造番书（西夏文），改服饰官制，强化主体性。
timeline.summary_en: He ordered Yeli Renrong and others to devise the Tangut script, reformed dress and officialdom, and asserted Xia distinctiveness.

timeline.title: 取瓜沙肃
timeline.summary: 攻取河西走廊要地，奠称帝版图基础。
timeline.summary_en: He seized key prefectures of the Hexi Corridor, laying the territorial base for his imperial claim.

timeline.title: 河西称帝
timeline.summary: 即皇帝位，国号大夏，改元，与宋辽并立。
timeline.summary_en: He took the imperial title under the dynastic name Great Xia, changed the era, and stood alongside Song and Liao.

timeline.title: 三川口之战
timeline.summary: 宋夏大战之一，夏军获胜。
timeline.summary_en: One of the great Song–Xia battles; Xia forces won.

timeline.title: 好水川大捷
timeline.summary: 宋夏大战中夏军重创宋军，确立西夏军事地位。
timeline.summary_en: Xia forces crushed the Song army, establishing Western Xia's military standing.

timeline.title: 定川寨之战
timeline.summary: 再创宋军，确立军事优势。
timeline.summary_en: Another heavy defeat for Song forces confirmed Xia's military edge.

timeline.title: 庆历和议
timeline.summary: 宋夏达成和议，元昊对宋称臣而自帝其国，换岁赐与边境稳定。
timeline.summary_en: Song and Xia made peace; Yuanhao styled himself a subject to Song while reigning as emperor at home, trading form for annual payments and border stability.

timeline.title: 辽夏和战
timeline.summary: 与辽冲突后和，宋辽夏三角外交。
timeline.summary_en: After clashes with Liao came peace—triangular diplomacy among Song, Liao, and Xia.

timeline.title: 没藏氏与后嗣
timeline.summary: 遇弑后幼主谅祚继立，外戚没藏氏格局形成。
timeline.summary_en: After the assassination the child ruler Liangzuo succeeded, and the consort clan Mozang came to power.

timeline.title: 遇弑
timeline.summary: 元昊在宫廷斗争中被刺死，西夏转入后续诸帝。
timeline.summary_en: Yuanhao was stabbed to death amid palace struggles; Western Xia passed to its later rulers.

timeline.title: 番汉官制

emperors.bio_md:
# 西夏景宗 · 主要事迹

李元昊是西夏实际的开国之主。1032 年父李德明卒，他袭夏王位，随即加速去宋化与民族国家建构；1038 年在兴庆府即皇帝位，国号大夏，改元天授礼法延祚，正式与宋、辽并立。本页以《宋史·卷485·夏国传》为年表主线，《辽史》相关纪为二手入口。

称帝前后，他完成了一整套国族符号与制度建构：命野利仁荣等造番书（西夏文），改服饰官制，又设中书、枢密等机构，番汉分号。这套"强化主体性"的路线，与[[n-wei-xiaowen|北魏孝文帝]]的汉化改革恰好方向相反，对读可见中古北方政权处理自身身份的两种极端路径。

武功方面，约 1036 年他攻取瓜、沙、肃等河西走廊要地，奠定称帝版图——这条走廊正是[[han-wu-di|汉武帝]]时代开通的西北命脉，千年之后成为大夏立国的根基。1040 年三川口、1041 年好水川、1042 年定川寨，夏军连续三年重创宋军，确立了西夏的军事地位；好水川一役尤为宋夏战争的名场面（互见《宋史》任福等列传）。

连战之后是外交收尾。1044 年宋夏达成庆历和议：元昊对宋称臣而自帝其国，以名实分离换取岁赐与边境稳定；同年与辽冲突后言和，在宋、辽、夏三角之间周旋得体。文治、武功、韬略三线，至此把一个河西政权立成了鼎立之一极。

1048 年，元昊在宫廷斗争中被刺死，幼主谅祚继立，外戚没藏氏掌权——国祚并未随他个人终结，西夏转入后续诸帝。需要说明的是，宋、辽史书对西夏站位偏贬，本项目月旦取中；西夏文创制等细节仍待专书补证。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Yuanhao was the de facto founder of Western Xia. In 1032 his father Li Deming died and he succeeded as Prince of Xia, at once accelerating de-Songification and nation-building; in 1038 he proclaimed himself emperor at Xingqing, took the dynastic name Great Xia, and changed the era to Tianshou Lifa Yanzuo, formally standing alongside Song and Liao. This page takes 《宋史·卷485·夏国传》 as the backbone of its chronology, with the relevant annals of 《辽史》 as a secondary entry point.

Around his proclamation he completed a whole set of national symbols and institutions: he ordered Yeli Renrong and others to devise the Tangut script, reformed dress and officialdom, and established organs such as the Secretariat and the Bureau of Military Affairs under separate Tangut and Han designations. This line of "asserting distinctiveness" ran in exactly the opposite direction from the sinicization of

; read together, they show the two extreme paths by which medieval northern regimes handled their own identity.

On the military side, around 1036 he seized Gua, Sha, Su, and other key points of the Hexi Corridor, laying the territorial foundation for his imperial claim—the very corridor opened in the age of

as the northwest lifeline, which a thousand years later became the ground on which Great Xia was founded. At Sanchuankou in 1040, Haoshuichuan in 1041, and Dingchuanzhai in 1042, Xia forces mauled the Song armies three years running and established Western Xia's military standing; Haoshuichuan in particular is the famous set piece of the Song–Xia war (cross-referenced in the biographies of Ren Fu and others in 《宋史》).

After the string of victories came the diplomatic wrap-up. In 1044 Song and Xia reached the Qingli settlement: Yuanhao styled himself a subject toward Song while reigning as emperor within his own realm, trading the split between name and fact for annual payments and a stable border; the same year, after clashes with Liao, he made peace, maneuvering deftly within the Song–Liao–Xia triangle. Civil construction, military success, and statecraft together had by now raised a Hexi regime into one pole of a tripartite standoff.

In 1048 Yuanhao was stabbed to death amid palace struggles; the child ruler Liangzuo succeeded, and the consort clan Mozang took power—the dynasty did not end with his person, and Western Xia passed to its later rulers. It should be noted that Song and Liao historiography is biased against Western Xia, so this project's appraisal takes a middle position; details such as the creation of the Tangut script still await confirmation from specialized scholarship.

emperors.bio_md:
# 南唐后主 · 主要事迹

李煜是南唐末主。宋建隆二年（961），中主李璟卒，李煜继位于金陵，此时南唐对宋已处劣势。本页以《宋史·卷478·南唐世家》为年表主线，《宋史·太祖纪》编年互见（本地参考库已备）。

开宝前后（971），他去帝号、称江南国主，对宋称臣以求苟安；在位间倾力于书画音律词章，文艺成就远超君道事功。

开宝七年（974），曹彬等率宋师南下伐江南，兵临长江；开宝八年（975）宋军破金陵，后主出降，南唐亡。此役出自[[n-song-tai-zu|宋太祖]]朝平江南的部署，可与宋方本纪对读。

开宝九年（976）他北迁汴京，封违命侯，软禁中词多故国之思。太平兴国三年（978）卒于京师，时宋太宗在位；民间有七夕赐牵机药传说，正史记载简略，此处作待考处理。

他的后效在文学：二主词为词史入口，君道失败与词人成就分离，后世月旦常带同情分。与南唐元宗（中主李璟）对读，可见南唐自中主至后主两代而终的格局。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Yu was the last ruler of the Southern Tang. In the second year of the Song Jianlong era (961), the Middle Ruler Li Jing died, and Li Yu succeeded to the throne at Jinling, with Southern Tang already at a disadvantage against the Song. This page takes 《宋史·卷478·南唐世家》 as the chronological backbone, cross-checked against the annals in 《宋史·太祖纪》 (available in the local reference library).

Around the Kaibao era (971), he renounced the imperial title, styled himself Ruler of Jiangnan, and submitted to the Song as a vassal in search of a precarious peace; throughout his reign he poured his energy into painting, calligraphy, music, and verse, and his literary achievement far outran his record as a sovereign.

In the seventh year of Kaibao (974), Cao Bin and others led the Song army south against Jiangnan and brought it to the banks of the Yangtze; in the eighth year (975) Song forces breached Jinling, the Last Ruler came out and surrendered, and Southern Tang fell. This campaign grew out of the Jiangnan strategy of

's court and can be read against the Song-side basic annals.

In the ninth year of Kaibao (976) he was moved north to Bianjing and enfeoffed as the Marquis of Weiming; in confinement his ci poems dwelled on longing for his lost realm. He died at the capital in the third year of Taiping Xingguo (978), while Emperor Taizong of Song was on the throne; a folk legend holds that poison was granted to him on the Double Seventh night, but the standard histories record little, and the matter is treated here as unverified.

His afterlife lies in literature: the ci of the Two Rulers are an entryway into the history of the genre, his failure as a sovereign is read apart from his achievement as a poet, and later judgment has often carried a measure of sympathy. Read alongside Southern Tang Yuanzong (the Middle Ruler Li Jing), the page shows the shape of a Southern Tang that ran its course in two generations, from the Middle Ruler to the Last Ruler.

emperors.summary: 受禅代周、灭陈混一南北，以开皇制度奠定后世政制底盘，却因晚年废立与二世而亡留下争议的开国之主。
emperors.summary_en: Founding ruler who received Northern Zhou's abdication to establish the Sui and destroyed Chen to reunify north and south, laying the institutional foundation for later dynasties through the Kaihuang system, yet left controversy through the late-life change of heir and the dynasty's fall in the second generation.

portrait.appearance_basis: 传统画像符号化描写居多。MVP 用占位图；定稿前依时代冠服作艺术想象。

timeline.title: 代周建隋
timeline.summary: 受北周禅让建隋，改元开皇，北周亡。
timeline.summary_en: He received Northern Zhou's abdication and founded the Sui, changing the era name to Kaihuang; Northern Zhou ended.

timeline.title: 尽灭北周宗室隐患
timeline.title_en: Purging the Northern Zhou Royal House
timeline.summary: 开国之初以政治清洗巩固新朝（克制叙述）。
timeline.summary_en: In the founding's early days he consolidated the new dynasty through political purges (restrained account).

timeline.title: 迁大兴城
timeline.summary: 营迁大兴（新长安），都城格局一新。
timeline.summary_en: He built and moved the capital to Daxing (the new Chang'an), giving the capital an entirely new layout.

timeline.title: 灭后梁
timeline.summary: 江陵后梁亡，为南进混一的前奏。
timeline.summary_en: The Later Liang at Jiangling fell, a prelude to the southern advance and reunification.

timeline.title: 灭陈混一
timeline.summary: 平陈，南北再统一，史称混一戎夏。
timeline.summary_en: Chen was pacified and north and south reunified, known in history as "the unification of the realm".

timeline.title: 江南反隋平定
timeline.summary: 灭陈后江南叛乱被平定，统一局面巩固。
timeline.summary_en: After Chen's fall, the Jiangnan rebellions were suppressed and the unified order was consolidated.

timeline.title: 废太子勇
timeline.summary: 废黜太子杨勇，储位动摇。
timeline.summary_en: Crown Prince Yang Yong was deposed, and the succession was shaken.

timeline.title: 废勇立广
timeline.summary: 立晋王广为太子，种下国祚风险。
timeline.summary_en: The Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, was made crown prince, planting a risk to the dynasty's fortunes.

timeline.title: 改元仁寿
timeline.summary: 晚年改元，储位已定。
timeline.summary_en: The era name was changed in his final years, with the heir already settled.

timeline.title: 仁寿宫事
timeline.summary: 卧病仁寿宫，遗命与继位过程史有异说（克制叙述）。
timeline.summary_en: He lay ill at Renshou Palace; the record diverges on his dying orders and the succession process (restrained account).

timeline.title: 文帝崩
timeline.summary: 崩于仁寿宫，炀帝即位；统一遗产与二世风险同时交接。
timeline.summary_en: He died at Renshou Palace and Emperor Yang ascended; the legacy of unification and the risk of a second-generation collapse were handed over together.

timeline.title: 开皇制度
timeline.summary: 三省六部成型、统一货币度量、检括户口，奠定后世政制底盘。
timeline.summary_en: The Three Departments and Six Ministries took shape, currency and weights and measures were unified, and households were registered and checked, laying the institutional foundation for later dynasties.

emperors.bio_md:
# 隋文帝 · 主要事迹

杨坚以受禅方式代北周建隋，改元开皇。新朝初立，一面以政治手段清除北周宗室隐患、稳住局面，一面营迁大兴城，重定都城格局——开国的前几步，走得谨慎而彻底。

开皇七年，江陵后梁亡，南进之门洞开；开皇九年平陈，自东晋以来近三百年的南北分裂宣告结束，史称「混一戎夏」。次年江南反隋势力被平定，统一局面真正巩固。灭陈一役虽由诸将执行，战略决断皆出朝廷。

混一之外，开皇间三省六部成型、统一货币度量、检括户口，奠定此后数百年的政制底盘，后效极高。论文治的制度遗产，隋文帝在历代开国之主中位置很靠前。

晚年却是另一番走向：开皇二十年废太子勇、改立晋王广，储位之争自此埋下国祚风险。仁寿四年，文帝崩于仁寿宫，遗命与继位过程史有异说。其子[[sui-yang|隋炀帝]]即位，统一遗产与二世风险同时交接——废立争议与「二世而亡」的结局，压低了后世对这场开国之局的评价。与[[qin-shi-huang|秦始皇]]对读：二者皆在长期分裂后完成混一，又皆在二代迅速陷入危局，是读统一帝国史绕不开的一对对照。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yang Jian replaced Northern Zhou and founded the Sui through an abdication, changing the era name to Kaihuang. With the new dynasty just established, he used political means to remove the lingering threat of the Northern Zhou royal house and steady the situation, while building and moving to Daxing and redesigning the capital's layout — the founding's first steps were taken with caution and thoroughness.

In Kaihuang 7, the Later Liang at Jiangling fell and the gate to the southern advance swung open; in Kaihuang 9 Chen was pacified, ending the nearly three-hundred-year division of north and south since the Eastern Jin — known in history as "the unification of the realm". The following year the anti-Sui forces in Jiangnan were suppressed, and the unified order was truly consolidated. Though the destruction of Chen was executed by his generals, every strategic decision came from the court.

Beyond unification, the Kaihuang era saw the Three Departments and Six Ministries take shape, currency and weights and measures unified, and households registered and checked — laying the institutional foundation of government for centuries to come, with exceptionally far-reaching aftereffects. In terms of institutional legacy, Emperor Wen ranks near the very front among the founding rulers of successive dynasties.

His later years took a different course: in Kaihuang 20 he deposed Crown Prince Yang Yong and installed the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, in his place — and the struggle over the succession thereafter planted a risk to the dynasty's fortunes. In Renshou 4, Emperor Wen died at Renshou Palace; the historical record diverges on his dying orders and the succession process. His son

took the throne, and the legacy of unification was handed over together with the risk of a second-generation collapse — the controversy over the change of heir and the ending of "falling in the second generation" lowered later generations' appraisal of this founding. Read alongside
: both completed reunification after long division, and both quickly plunged into crisis in the second generation — an unavoidable pair for anyone reading the history of unified empires.

emperors.bio_md:
# 隋炀帝 · 主要事迹

杨广本为晋王，开皇九年（589）参与平陈立功，开皇二十年（600）被立为太子，仁寿四年（604）即帝位，后改元大业。本页以《隋书·炀帝纪》为年表主线，辅以《资治通鉴·隋纪》编年对照。

大业年间他接连启动超大规模的工程与行动：大业元年（605）营建东都洛阳，开通济渠等运河段，贯通南北水运；大业四年（608）又开永济渠北通涿郡；大业五年（609）西巡张掖，西域胡商前来朝会，一时呈现盛世表象。东都与运河构成他最重要的后效遗产，但征发之巨也同步消耗着帝国的根本。

转折出现在大业八年（612）一征高句丽：大举东征，丧师费财，国内矛盾激化。次年（613）再征辽东，杨玄感起兵，崩坏加速。大业十二年（616）他三幸江都，中原随之失控；大业十三年（617）群雄并起，中枢名存实亡；大业十四年（618），宇文化及等发动江都之变，炀帝身死，隋亡。

后世对他月旦极低，而运河、东都与沟通南北的后效深远。与[[sui-wen|隋文帝]]对读，可见开皇一朝的积累如何在大业年间被推向极致并耗尽；与[[tang-tai-zong|唐太宗]]对读，可见唐承隋制的承接与反拨。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yang Guang was originally the Prince of Jin. In Kaihuang 9 (589) he took part in the pacification of Chen and earned merit; in Kaihuang 20 (600) he was made crown prince; in Renshou 4 (604) he ascended the throne, later changing the era name to Daye. This page follows the Annals of Emperor Yang in the Book of Sui as its chronological spine, cross-checked against the Sui chapters of the Zizhi Tongjian.

During the Daye era he launched one outsized project and operation after another: in Daye 1 (605) he built the Eastern Capital at Luoyang and dug the Tongji Canal and other canal sections, linking north-south water transport; in Daye 4 (608) he dug the Yongji Canal, reaching Zhuo Commandery in the north; in Daye 5 (609) he toured west to Zhangye, where Hu merchants from the Western Regions came to court, presenting for a time the appearance of a flourishing age. The Eastern Capital and the canals form his most important lasting legacy, yet the sheer scale of conscription was simultaneously consuming the empire's foundations.

The turning point came in Daye 8 (612) with the first campaign against Goguryeo: a massive eastern expedition that lost armies and drained wealth, intensifying domestic tensions. The following year (613) he campaigned in Liaodong again, and Yang Xuangan rose in revolt, accelerating the collapse. In Daye 12 (616) he went to Jiangdu for the third time, and the Central Plains slipped from control; in Daye 13 (617) warlords rose on all sides and the central authority existed in name only; in Daye 14 (618), Yuwen Huaji and others launched the Jiangdu coup, Emperor Yang was killed, and the Sui fell.

Later generations judged him extremely harshly, yet the lasting effects of the canals, the Eastern Capital, and the linking of north and south run deep. Read alongside
, one can see how the accumulation of the Kaihuang era was pushed to the extreme and exhausted during the Daye years; read alongside
, one can see how the Tang both inherited and reacted against Sui institutions.

# 唐太宗 · 主要事迹

李世民以秦王定天下、以玄武门入承大统，贞观一朝以用人与纳谏闻名，并在北境与辽东方向留下清晰的军事地理轨迹。本页主据两唐书太宗本纪与《资治通鉴·唐纪》（本地参考库已备；旧/新唐书 PDF 请自行核验完整性）。

本图鉴同时收录其即位前关键节点（晋阳起兵），以便地图连成一条「从河东到长安、再向北与东」的人生线。与[[han-wu-di|汉武帝]]对读，可看不同时代的「极盛叙事」；与[[qin-shi-huang|秦始皇]]对读，可看统一帝国传统下治理风格的差异。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Shimin secured the realm as Prince of Qin and entered the succession through the Xuanwu Gate Incident; the Zhenguan reign became famous for its employment of talent and acceptance of remonstrance, and left a clear military-geographic track on the northern frontier and in the Liaodong direction. This page draws mainly on the Taizong annals of the two Tang histories and the Tang chapters of the Zizhi Tongjian (available in the local reference library; please verify the completeness of the Old/New Book of Tang PDFs yourself).

This atlas also includes the key node before his enthronement (the Jinyang uprising), so that the map connects into a single life line running "from Hedong to Chang'an, then north and east". Read alongside
, one can see the "narratives of zenith" of different eras; read alongside
, one can see the differences in governing style within the unified-empire tradition.

emperors.bio_md:
# 武则天 · 主要事迹

武则天是中国史上唯一正式称帝的女皇帝。本页以《旧唐书·则天皇后本纪》为年表主线，辅以《新唐书》与《资治通鉴·唐纪》编年（本地参考库已备）。她贞观十一年入宫为[[tang-tai-zong|唐太宗]]才人，历感业寺环节后重返宫廷，永徽六年由昭仪立为皇后——废王立武之争中，长孙无忌等元老反对派相继贬死，她由此进入权力中枢。

显庆五年后高宗多病，天后参决政务，朝中形成"二圣"格局。弘道元年高宗崩于洛阳，中宗即位，她临朝称制；次年即废中宗为庐陵王，改立睿宗而实掌朝政。垂拱四年洛阳明堂建成，铜匦告密与酷吏政治并行，恩威双轨的统治术于此成型。

天授元年，她在神都洛阳加尊号、改国号为周，正式称帝，女主称制由事实变为名分。在位期间破格用人、发展科举殿试，神功元年狄仁杰入相成为能吏政治的代表节点；文治实绩与酷吏之治始终并存，构成武周的一体两面。

神龙元年，张柬之等发动政变拥中宗复位，武周终结，则天迁宫。旧史多以"女祸"叙事贬抑，今人则更重估其制度与人事遗产——本图鉴月旦中性偏下，留给读者对读：从入宫才人到革唐为周，再到还政李唐，与[[tang-xian-zong|唐宪宗]]的中兴对照，可见唐室中衰与重建的完整弧线。

bio_parts_en.value: Wu Zetian is the only woman in Chinese history to have formally taken the imperial title. This page builds its chronology on the "Basic Annals of Empress Zetian" in the Old Book of Tang, supplemented by the New Book of Tang and the Tang chronicle of the Zizhi Tongjian (all held in the local reference library). She entered the palace in Zhenguan 11 as a cairen consort of

and, after the Ganye Temple episode, returned to the court; in Yonghui 6 she was raised from zhaoyi to empress. In the struggle over deposing Empress Wang for Wu, veteran opponents such as Zhangsun Wuji were demoted and died one after another, and through this she entered the center of power.

After Xianqing 5, as Gaozong fell frequently ill, the Heavenly Empress joined in deciding state affairs and a "Two Sages" arrangement took shape at court. In Hongdao 1 Gaozong died in Luoyang; Zhongzong succeeded and she ruled from behind the screen. The very next year she deposed Zhongzong to Prince of Luling, installed Ruizong instead, and held real power over the court. In Chuigong 4 the Bright Hall in Luoyang was completed, while copper-box informant reports and the politics of harsh officials ran in tandem: her dual-track statecraft of favor and fear took form here.

In Tianshou 1, at the Divine Capital Luoyang, she took a new honorific title, changed the dynastic name to Zhou, and formally assumed the throne; rule by a female sovereign passed from fact into name. During her reign she broke conventions in appointing talent and developed the palace examination within the imperial examinations, and in Shengong 1 Di Renjie's entry as chancellor became the representative node of capable-official politics. Solid civil achievements and the rule of harsh officials coexisted throughout, forming the two faces of Wu Zhou.

In Shenlong 1, Zhang Jianzhi and others launched a coup that restored Zhongzong; Wu Zhou ended and Zetian moved to another palace. The old histories mostly belittled her through the "female calamity" narrative, while today her institutional and personnel legacy is being revalued. This atlas's appraisal is neutral to mildly negative, left for readers to weigh against the evidence: from palace cairen to changing Tang into Zhou and then returning power to the Li Tang house, read alongside the restoration of
, one can see the full arc of the Tang house's mid-course decline and rebuilding.

timeline.summary: 顺宗内禅，即帝位；朝廷人事与年号随之更始，明年改元元和。
timeline.summary_en: Shunzong abdicates within the family and he takes the throne; court personnel and the era name are renewed, and the next year changes to Yuanhe.

timeline.title: 平夏绥杨惠琳
timeline.summary: 讨平夏绥杨惠琳，削藩早期胜利。
timeline.summary_en: Suppresses Yang Huilin of Xia-Sui, an early victory in reducing the provinces.

timeline.title: 平西川
timeline.summary: 讨平西川刘辟，展示削藩决心。
timeline.summary_en: Suppresses Liu Pi of Xichuan, demonstrating the resolve to reduce the provinces.

timeline.title: 成德王承宗战事
timeline.summary: 讨成德王承宗，成果有限，显示削藩难度。
timeline.summary_en: Campaigns against Wang Chengzong of Chengde with limited results, showing how hard province reduction is.

timeline.title: 李师道刺武元衡
timeline.summary: 藩镇以恐怖手段刺杀宰相武元衡于长安，朝野震动。
timeline.summary_en: A military province has the chancellor Wu Yuanheng assassinated in Chang'an by terror tactics, shocking court and country.

timeline.title: 裴度宣慰淮西
timeline.summary: 宰相裴度赴淮西督师宣慰，为雪夜入蔡的政治背景。
timeline.summary_en: Chancellor Pei Du goes to Huaixi to direct and reassure the armies, the political backdrop to the snowy-night entry into Cai.

timeline.title: 平淮西
timeline.summary: 李愬雪夜入蔡州，擒吴元济，元和削藩达到高潮。
timeline.summary_en: Li Su enters Caizhou on a snowy night and captures Wu Yuanji, the high point of Yuanhe province reduction.

timeline.title: 成德归朝
timeline.summary: 成德等河朔藩镇一度听命朝廷，元和中兴气象达到高点。
timeline.summary_en: Chengde and other Heshuo provinces for a time obey the court, and the Yuanhe Restoration reaches its peak.

timeline.title: 迎佛骨
timeline.summary: 迎法门寺佛骨入长安；韩愈上表极谏，贬逐出京。
timeline.summary_en: The Famen Temple Buddha relic is received into Chang'an; Han Yu submits a memorial of utmost remonstrance and is banished from the capital.

timeline.title: 穆宗即位
timeline.summary: 宪宗崩后穆宗立，朝廷人事与年号更始，削藩回落。
timeline.summary_en: After Xianzong's death Muzong succeeds; court personnel and the era name are renewed, and province reduction recedes.

timeline.title: 暴崩
timeline.summary: 暴崩于长安，史载与宦官相关的疑云，削藩成果随之回落。
timeline.summary_en: Dies suddenly in Chang'an; the histories record suspicions involving eunuchs, and the gains of province reduction recede.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐宪宗 · 主要事迹

李纯在位十五年（805—820），年号元和，是安史之乱后唐朝最有振作气象的皇帝。本页以《旧唐书·宪宗纪》为年表主线，辅以《新唐书·宪宗纪》与《资治通鉴》编年对照（本地参考库已备）。他的一生主线只有两个字：削藩。

元和元年（806）是他开局的手笔：先是讨平夏绥杨惠琳，继而讨平西川刘辟——两战皆捷，向天下藩镇展示了朝廷不再姑息的决心。但元和四年（809）讨伐成德王承宗一役成果有限，也让他看清河朔藩镇根深蒂固、硬啃不易的现实。

真正的考验在淮西。元和十年（815），平卢李师道竟遣刺客在长安街头杀死主战宰相武元衡，朝野震动，而朝廷用兵之志未移。元和十二年（817），宰相裴度亲赴淮西宣慰督师，名将李愬雪夜奇袭入蔡州，生擒吴元济——这是元和削藩的高潮，也是中唐最著名的一场奇袭。次年（818）前后，成德等河朔强藩一度听命于朝，史称"元和中兴"。

晚年他迎法门寺佛骨入长安，韩愈上表极谏而被贬，留下君臣关系与信仰政策的另一面相。元和十五年（820），他在长安暴崩，史载此事笼罩着与宦官相关的疑云；唐穆宗即位后，削藩成果迅速回落，河朔此后复叛。从唐顺宗的永贞内禅开局，到暴崩落幕，"元和中兴"是否可持续，正是读宪宗一朝最值得停下来的问题；与[[tang-tai-zong|唐太宗]]的贞观范式对读，也可见盛唐与中唐之间帝国处境的巨大落差。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Chun reigned for fifteen years (805–820) under the era name Yuanhe and was the most revitalizing emperor of the Tang after the An Lushan Rebellion. This page builds its chronology on the "Annals of Xianzong" in the Old Book of Tang, checked against the "Annals of Xianzong" in the New Book of Tang and the Zizhi Tongjian (all held in the local reference library). The main line of his life comes down to two words: reducing the provinces.

Yuanhe 1 (806) showed his opening hand: first he suppressed Yang Huilin of Xia-Sui, then Liu Pi of Xichuan. Two victories in a row announced to every military province that the court would no longer be lenient. But the campaign against Wang Chengzong of Chengde in Yuanhe 4 (809) achieved limited results, and it taught him how deeply entrenched the Heshuo provinces were and how hard they would be to crack.

The real test was Huaixi. In Yuanhe 10 (815), Li Shidao of Pinglu sent assassins who killed the pro-war chancellor Wu Yuanheng in the streets of Chang'an, shocking court and country, yet the court's will to use force did not waver. In Yuanhe 12 (817) the chancellor Pei Du went in person to Huaixi to reassure and direct the armies, and the renowned general Li Su made a surprise entry into Caizhou on a snowy night and captured Wu Yuanji alive: the climax of Yuanhe province reduction and the most celebrated surprise attack of the mid-Tang. Around the following year (818), powerful Heshuo provinces such as Chengde for a time obeyed the court, in what the histories call the "Yuanhe Restoration."

In his later years he received the Buddha's relic from Famen Temple into Chang'an; Han Yu submitted a memorial of utmost remonstrance and was banished, leaving another face of ruler-minister relations and religious policy. In Yuanhe 15 (820) he died suddenly in Chang'an, an event the histories record as wrapped in suspicions involving eunuchs. After Emperor Muzong of Tang took the throne, the gains of province reduction quickly receded and Heshuo rebelled again. From the Yongzhen abdication of Shunzong at the opening to the sudden death at the close, whether the "Yuanhe Restoration" could have lasted is the question most worth pausing over in Xianzong's reign; read against the Zhenguan model of
, it also shows the enormous gap in the empire's circumstances between the High Tang and the mid-Tang.

emperors.summary: 在位六年，高平破敌、三征淮南、北伐收复三关，以整军与改革为北宋统一奠基的英年早逝之主。
emperors.summary_en: An emperor who died young after only six years on the throne, breaking the enemy at Gaoping, campaigning thrice in Huainan, and recovering the Three Passes in a northern expedition, whose military reorganization and reforms laid the foundation for Northern Song unification.

timeline.title: 即位
timeline.summary: 郭威崩，柴荣即位，是为世宗。
timeline.summary_en: Guo Wei dies and Chai Rong takes the throne, becoming Shizong.

timeline.title: 沿用显德年号
timeline.summary: 郭威正月改广顺四年为显德元年；荣即位后沿用，朝廷人事更始。
timeline.summary_en: Guo Wei changes Guangshun 4 into Xiande 1 in the first month; Chai Rong keeps it after his accession as court personnel are renewed.

timeline.title: 高平之战
timeline.summary: 亲征败北汉、契丹联军于高平，战后整肃禁军，确立权威。
timeline.summary_en: Campaigns in person and defeats the allied Northern Han and Khitan army at Gaoping, then purges the palace army and establishes his authority.

timeline.title: 毁佛铸钱
timeline.summary: 限寺减僧，毁铜佛铸钱，以充财政军备。
timeline.summary_en: Restricts temples and reduces the clergy, melting bronze Buddha statues for coin to fund finances and armament.

timeline.title: 整军均田
timeline.summary: 选练禁军、限制寺院、均定田赋，国力回升。
timeline.summary_en: Selects and trains the palace army, restricts temples, and equalizes land taxes; state power recovers.

timeline.title: 征淮南
timeline.summary: 亲征南唐，显德振旅。
timeline.summary_en: Campaigns in person against Southern Tang; the Xiande armies are invigorated.

timeline.title: 经略淮南
timeline.summary: 多次征南唐，南压强敌，指向江北诸州。
timeline.summary_en: Campaigns repeatedly against Southern Tang, pressing the strong enemy in the south toward the prefectures north of the river.

timeline.title: 江北十四州
timeline.summary: 南唐献江北之地，周取十四州。
timeline.summary_en: Southern Tang cedes the lands north of the river and Zhou takes fourteen prefectures.

timeline.title: 北伐契丹
timeline.summary: 亲率北伐，收复关南部分州县，病重回师。
timeline.summary_en: Leads the northern expedition in person, recovers some Guannan prefectures, and returns gravely ill.

timeline.title: 收复三关
timeline.summary: 北伐取关南三州，混一之志未竟而病重。
timeline.summary_en: The northern expedition takes three prefectures in Guannan; his ambition to unify goes unfulfilled as his illness worsens.

timeline.title: 遗命范质等
timeline.summary: 病重托孤于范质等，身后旋有陈桥之变。
timeline.summary_en: Gravely ill, he entrusts his heir to Fan Zhi and others; the Chenqiao Mutiny follows soon after his death.

timeline.title: 世宗崩
timeline.summary: 崩于开封，子宗训年幼继位，旋有陈桥兵变，周禅于宋。
timeline.summary_en: Dies at Kaifeng; his young son Zongxun succeeds, the Chenqiao Mutiny soon follows, and Zhou yields to Song.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后周世宗 · 主要事迹

柴荣在位不过六年，却是五代末局里承前启后的枢纽：上接养父后周太祖郭威的草创之业，下开[[n-song-tai-zu|宋太祖]]赵匡胤的统一之局。本页以《旧五代史·周书·世宗纪》为年表主线，辅以《新五代史·周本纪》与《资治通鉴》编年（本地参考库已备）。

显德元年，郭威崩，柴荣即位，沿用显德年号。北汉与契丹联军压境，他亲征迎战，败之于高平，战后整肃禁军，一战确立新君权威。内政上同样果决：显德二年限寺减僧、毁铜佛铸钱以充财政军备；显德间又选练禁军、均定田赋，使国力回升。

南方，他连年亲征南唐，显德三年起兵，四至五年间反复经略淮南，至显德五年南唐献出江北之地，周取十四州，把疆界推到长江北岸——这正是后来[[n-tang-houzhu|南唐后主]]一系被动局面的先声。显德六年，他转而北伐契丹，收复关南三关州县，兵锋直指幽州方向，却于军中病重，只得回师。

回到开封后，他托孤于范质等，旋即驾崩，子宗训年幼继位。次年陈桥兵变，周禅于宋，他未竟的混一之志由宋人接手完成。史家每论其英年早逝：若得永年，宋史的开局或许改写——这桩假设，正是读五代末史时最耐人寻味的关节。

bio_parts_en.value: Chai Rong reigned barely six years, yet he was the hinge between what came before and after at the close of the Five Dynasties: he inherited the newly founded enterprise of his adoptive father Guo Wei, Taizu of Later Zhou, and opened the way to the unification completed under

Zhao Kuangyin. This page builds its chronology on the "Annals of Shizong" in the Zhou shu of the Old History of the Five Dynasties, supplemented by the "Zhou Basic Annals" in the New History of the Five Dynasties and the Zizhi Tongjian (all held in the local reference library).

In Xiande 1 Guo Wei died and Chai Rong succeeded, keeping the Xiande era name. When the allied armies of Northern Han and the Khitans pressed the border, he campaigned in person and defeated them at Gaoping; after the battle he purged and reorganized the palace army, establishing a new ruler's authority in a single stroke. His domestic policy was equally decisive: in Xiande 2 he restricted temples, reduced the clergy, and melted bronze Buddha statues for coin to fund finances and armament; across the Xiande years he further selected and trained the palace army and equalized land taxes, bringing state power back up.

In the south he campaigned against Southern Tang year after year, raising armies in Xiande 3 and maneuvering repeatedly in Huainan through Xiande 4 and 5, until in Xiande 5 Southern Tang ceded the lands north of the river and Zhou took fourteen prefectures, pushing the frontier to the north bank of the Yangzi, the very precursor of the passive position later faced by the line of

bio_parts_en.label: Li Yu, last ruler of Southern Tang

bio_parts_en.value:
. In Xiande 6 he turned to a northern expedition against the Khitans, recovered the Three Passes and prefectures of Guannan with his spearhead pointed toward Youzhou, but fell gravely ill in the field and had to turn back.

Back in Kaifeng he entrusted his young heir to Fan Zhi and others and died soon after; his son Zongxun succeeded as a child. The next year came the Chenqiao Mutiny, and Zhou yielded to Song; his unfinished ambition of unification was taken up and completed by the Song. Historians often dwell on his early death: had he been granted long years, the opening chapter of Song history might have been rewritten. That counterfactual is the most thought-provoking knot in reading the history of the late Five Dynasties.

emperors.summary_en: The founding emperor who replaced the Zhou and founded the Song through the Chenqiao Mutiny, released his generals' military power over a cup of wine to strengthen the trunk and weaken the branches, and pacified the rival states south first and north later.

timeline.title: 陈桥兵变
timeline.summary: 兵变黄袍加身，代周建宋，定都开封。陈桥是否预谋为争议层。
timeline.summary_en: The mutiny draped him in the yellow robe; he replaced the Zhou, founded the Song, and fixed the capital at Kaifeng, though whether Chenqiao was premeditated remains disputed.

timeline.title: 定都开封
timeline.summary: 宋都汴京，五代积习上的新朝。
timeline.summary_en: The Song made Bianjing its capital, a new dynasty built on the accumulated habits of the Five Dynasties.

timeline.title: 杯酒释兵权
timeline.title_en: Dismissal over a Cup of Wine
timeline.summary: 以酒宴方式解除禁军宿将兵权，强干弱枝开端；细节有演绎。
timeline.summary_en: Over a wine banquet he stripped veteran palace-army generals of their commands, opening the path of strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches; the details have been embellished in later retellings.

timeline.summary_en: Murong Yanzhao and others pacified Hunan and Jingnan, the first step of the south-first, north-later plan.

timeline.title: 灭后蜀
timeline.summary: 王全斌等灭蜀。
timeline.summary_en: Wang Quanbin and others destroyed Later Shu.

timeline.summary: 潘美等灭南汉，岭南入宋。

timeline.title: 灭南唐
timeline.summary: 曹彬平江南，李煜降。
timeline.summary_en: Cao Bin pacified Jiangnan, and Li Yu surrendered.

timeline.title: 太祖崩
timeline.summary: 崩于开封，在位结束；「烛影斧声」等为争议层，轻点不坐实。
timeline.summary_en: He died at Kaifeng and his reign ended; tales such as "the candle shadow and the axe sound" belong to the disputed layer, touched on lightly rather than asserted as fact.

timeline.title: 太宗即位
timeline.summary: 太宗立，朝廷人事与年号随之更始；金匮之盟为争议层。
timeline.summary_en: Taizong took the throne, and court personnel and the era name began anew; the Golden Coffer Pact belongs to the disputed layer.

timeline.title: 先南后北
timeline.summary: 平荆湖、后蜀、南汉、南唐等，统一南方战略。
timeline.summary_en: He pacified Jinghu, Later Shu, Southern Han, Southern Tang, and others, a strategy of unifying the south.

timeline.title: 强干弱枝
timeline.summary: 收精兵、分事权，宋代国势路径。
timeline.summary_en: He gathered in elite troops and divided administrative authority, the Song dynasty's path of state power.

timeline.title: 重文抑武
timeline.summary: 抬高文官、分化兵权，奠定宋代国势路径。
timeline.summary_en: He elevated civil officials and split military authority, laying the Song dynasty's path of state power.

emperors.bio_md:
# 宋太祖 · 主要事迹

赵匡胤本是后周禁军将领，为[[zhou-shi|后周世宗]]旧部。建隆元年（960），陈桥驿兵变黄袍加身，代周建宋，定都开封——一个立在五代积习之上的新朝，就此登场。兵变是否预谋，史有争议，此处只作悬置。

开国之后的第一道难题是兵权。建隆二年（961），以酒宴方式解除禁军宿将兵权，即所谓「杯酒释兵权」；其细节后世多有演绎，但收精兵、分事权的方向由此确定。配合抬高文官、分化兵权的安排，「强干弱枝」「重文抑武」成为宋代国势的长期路径，影响远超太祖一朝。

统一战争取「先南后北」之策：建隆四年（963）慕容延钊等平荆湖，乾德三年（965）王全斌等灭后蜀，开宝四年（971）潘美等灭南汉，开宝八年（975）曹彬平江南，[[n-tang-houzhu|南唐后主李煜]]降。南方诸国次第入宋，五代以来的分裂格局大体收束。

开宝九年（976），太祖崩于开封，其弟宋太宗即位。「烛影斧声」「金匮之盟」历来是这一交接的争议层，本页只点到，不作坐实。

bio_parts_en.value: Zhao Kuangyin was originally a general of the Later Zhou palace armies and an old subordinate of

. In the first year of Jianlong (960), the mutiny at Chenqiao Station draped him in the yellow robe; he replaced the Zhou and founded the Song, fixing the capital at Kaifeng — a new dynasty standing atop the accumulated habits of the Five Dynasties had made its entrance. Whether the mutiny was premeditated is disputed in the sources and is left open here.

The first hard problem after the founding was military command. In the second year of Jianlong (961), he relieved the veteran generals of the palace armies of their commands over a wine banquet — the so-called "release of military power over a cup of wine." Its details have been much embellished by later generations, but the direction of concentrating elite troops and dividing authority was set from then on. Together with arrangements that elevated civil officials and split up military power, "strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches" and "exalting the civil and restraining the military" became the Song dynasty's long-term path of state power, with an influence reaching far beyond Taizu's own reign.

The wars of unification followed a "south first, north later" strategy: in the fourth year of Jianlong (963), Murong Yanzhao and others pacified Jinghu; in the third year of Qiande (965), Wang Quanbin and others destroyed Later Shu; in the fourth year of Kaibao (971), Pan Mei and others destroyed Southern Han; and in the eighth year of Kaibao (975), Cao Bin pacified Jiangnan, where

bio_parts_en.label: Li Yu, Last Ruler of Southern Tang

bio_parts_en.value:
surrendered. The southern states entered the Song one after another, and the fragmentation left over from the Five Dynasties was largely brought to a close.

In the ninth year of Kaibao (976), Taizu died at Kaifeng, and his younger brother, Emperor Taizong of Song, took the throne. "The shadow of a candle and the sound of an axe" and the "Golden Coffer Pact" have long been the disputed layers of this succession; this page points to them without settling them as fact.

emperors.summary: 灭宋完成大一统，建国号大元、定都大都，以行省与站赤制度塑造后世格局的征服王朝皇帝。
emperors.summary_en: A conquest-dynasty emperor who destroyed the Song to complete a grand unification, proclaimed the dynastic name Great Yuan, fixed the capital at Dadu, and shaped later ages through the provincial and postal-relay systems.

portrait.appearance_basis: 传统画像符号化描写居多。MVP 用占位图；定稿前依时代冠服作艺术想象。

timeline.title: 开平即位
timeline.summary: 即大汗位，建元中统，朝廷人事与年号随之更始。
timeline.summary_en: He took the throne as Great Khan and established the Zhongtong era; court personnel and the era name began anew.

timeline.title: 与阿里不哥争位
timeline.summary: 汗位内战，忽必烈胜。
timeline.summary_en: A civil war over the khanship ended in Kublai's victory.

timeline.title: 改元至元
timeline.summary: 中统改至元，汉地制度推进。
timeline.summary_en: Zhongtong was changed to Zhiyuan, and institutions for the Chinese territories advanced.

timeline.title: 建国号元
timeline.summary: 取《易》「大哉乾元」之义，建国号大元。
timeline.summary_en: Taking the sense of the Yijing line "great is the qian origin," he proclaimed the dynastic name Great Yuan.

timeline.title: 都于大都
timeline.summary: 改中都为大都，政治中心落于燕地。
timeline.summary_en: Zhongdu was renamed Dadu, and the political center settled in the land of Yan.

timeline.title: 襄樊破
timeline.summary: 襄阳破，灭宋关键节点。
timeline.summary_en: Xiangyang fell, the key turning point in the destruction of the Song.
sources: 宋史·度宗纪/瀛国公纪（对照）

timeline.title: 下临安
timeline.summary: 伯颜入临安，宋廷降，残部入海。
timeline.summary_en: Bayan entered Lin'an, the Song court surrendered, and the remnants fled to the sea.

timeline.title: 崖山灭宋
timeline.summary: 崖山之战，宋亡，中国再度大一统于元。
timeline.summary_en: At the Battle of Yashan the Song fell, and China was unified once again under the Yuan.

timeline.title: 再征日本失败
timeline.summary: 东征舰队风灾，扩张受挫。
timeline.summary_en: The eastern expedition fleet met a storm disaster, and expansion suffered a setback.

timeline.title: 世祖崩
timeline.summary: 成宗继，混一格局延续。
timeline.summary_en: Chengzong succeeded him, and the unified order continued.

timeline.title: 行省与站赤
timeline.summary: 行省制、驿站网络等，塑造后世行政区与交通遗产。
timeline.summary_en: The provincial system and the postal-relay station network shaped the administrative divisions and transport legacy of later ages.

emperors.bio_md:
# 元世祖 · 主要事迹

忽必烈是把蒙古汗国改写为中原式王朝、并完成唐亡以来再度大一统的皇帝。本页以《元史·世祖本纪》（卷004–017）为年表主线，平宋一段辅以《宋史·瀛国公纪》《二王本纪》对照（本地参考库已备）。

他的开局是一场汗位内战：中统元年（1260）即大汗位于开平，建元中统，随即与阿里不哥争位并胜出。此后汉地制度逐步推进：至元元年（1264）改元，至元八年（1271）取《易》「大哉乾元」之义建国号大元，至元九年（1272）改中都为大都，政治中心落定燕地。

灭宋是其在位中段的主线：至元十年（1273）襄阳破，打开南下关键节点；至元十三年（1276）伯颜入临安，宋廷降，残部入海；至元十六年（1279）崖山之战，宋亡，中国再度大一统于元。与[[qin-shi-huang|秦始皇]]对读，可见两次大一统之间的长线呼应；与[[n-song-tai-zu|宋太祖]]对读，则见赵宋开国与终结的首尾。

他的武功也有边界：至元十八年（1281）再征日本，东征舰队遇风灾而败，扩张受挫。真正影响后世更深的是制度遗产——行省制与站赤驿站网络塑造了后世的行政区划与交通格局。至元三十一年（1294）世祖崩于大都，成宗继立，混一格局延续。对这位征服王朝皇帝，正统与汉地治理的评价历来撕裂，本页取中性叙述，其历史后效则无可争议。

bio_parts_en.value:
Kublai was the emperor who rewrote the Mongol khanate into a Chinese-style dynasty and completed the first grand unification since the fall of the Tang. This page takes 《元史·世祖本纪》 (juan 004–017) as its chronological backbone, with the conquest of the Song cross-checked against 《宋史·瀛国公纪》 and 《二王本纪》 (available in the local reference library).

His opening act was a civil war over the khanship: in the first year of Zhongtong (1260) he took the throne as Great Khan at Kaiping and established the Zhongtong era, then immediately fought Ariq Böke for the succession and prevailed. Institutions for the Chinese territories advanced step by step thereafter: the era name changed in the first year of Zhiyuan (1264); in the eighth year of Zhiyuan (1271), taking the Yijing phrase "great is the qian origin," he proclaimed the dynastic name Great Yuan; and in the ninth year of Zhiyuan (1272) Zhongdu was renamed Dadu, fixing the political center in the land of Yan.

The destruction of the Song was the main thread of the middle of his reign: in the tenth year of Zhiyuan (1273) Xiangyang fell, opening the decisive gateway to the south; in the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan (1276) Bayan entered Lin'an, the Song court surrendered, and its remnants fled to the sea; and in the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan (1279) came the Battle of Yashan — the Song fell, and China was unified once more under the Yuan. Read against
, the page shows the long-range echo between two grand unifications; read against

, it shows the beginning and the end of the Zhao Song house.

His military reach also had its limits: in the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan (1281) he campaigned against Japan a second time, the eastern expedition fleet met a storm and was lost, and expansion suffered a check. What shaped later ages more deeply was the institutional legacy — the provincial (xingsheng) system and the zhanchi postal-relay network molded the administrative divisions and transport patterns of later dynasties. In the thirty-first year of Zhiyuan (1294) Shizu died at Dadu; Chengzong succeeded him, and the unified order continued. Assessments of this conquest-dynasty emperor — on legitimacy and on the governance of the Chinese territories — have long been sharply divided; this page adopts a neutral account, while his historical after-effects are beyond dispute.
